item.title: AI boom threatens circuit board crunch to rival pandemic-era chip shortage
item.description: The electronics industry faces a printed circuit board (PCB) shortage that could rival the pandemic-era chip crunch – with AI once again accused of hogging supplies. The Global Electronics Association says demand is arriving "at a scale the supply chain was not built for," straining everything from glass fabric and resin to finished boards. Its report, " The PCB Squeeze: A Wake-Up Call for Global Electronics ," says AI servers need increasingly complex boards. While a typical PC board has about 12 layers of tracks, AI server boards can have 40 to 60 layers or more, and each additional layer requires more resin, copper foil, and laminate. The supply of materials is set to be constrained through at least the first half of 2027, the report says, with meaningful relief unlikely before mid-2028. Programs to deliver PCBs for automotive, industrial, medical and even the defense industries are being crowded out as AI soaks up scarce capacity, it claims. The association's North American figures show orders growing much faster than deliveries. PCB bookings rose 56.1 percent in the first nine months of 2026 compared with the same period last year, while PCB shipments increased 13.3 percent. Fabrication capacity is expanding, aimed at meeting the increased demand from the AI infrastructure sector, especially in Asia, where more than 90 percent of the world's boards are made. The report says that $10 billion has gone toward new PCB plants in Southeast Asia, and at least as much has been invested in China over the past three years, but the raw materials are themselves constrained. It warns of lengthening lead times for those raw materials. Standard FR-4 laminate now takes six to eight weeks to ship, up from two to three weeks a year ago, while advanced low-loss laminates now take 14 to 18 weeks for delivery, for example. Tightening supplies usually lead to price increases, and the report says that suppliers raised laminate costs by 30 percent in September, and that the price tag of some types of E-glass cloth for circuit boards has risen by 300 percent. The report also puts copper prices up 37 percent over the past year. Concerns have been raised about copper supplies before, as The Register has reported multiple times. The association compares the risk with the 2021 chip shortage , when disrupted supplies left manufacturers unable to secure even relatively mundane components. New capacity is coming, but it is late and comes in dribs and drabs, according to the report, while AI demand just keeps on absorbing it as soon as it arrives. The association's advice is for buyers to plan early, and to share realistic forecasts with suppliers rather than double-booking. Board makers should qualify alternative suppliers of materials such as laminate and copper foil before shortages bite, but it warns against stockpiling beyond real need, which adds to forward-buying pressure. But it would like governments to step in, of course, by tracking board and material lead times

item.title: Bitcoin Price Crashes to $59,000 as Market Selloff Deepens
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Crashes to $59,000 as Market Selloff Deepens The bitcoin price crashed below $60,000 on Friday for the first time since early July, falling about $1,800 in roughly an hour as a deepening U.S. tech stock selloff dragged risk assets lower. Bitcoin traded near $61,400 at 9:40 a.m. ET and slid to about $59,600 by 10:45 a.m., a drop of nearly 3%, according to Look Into Bitcoin data . The bitcoin price is down about $3,400, or more than 5%, from the same time Thursday, when it traded near $63,000. The break of $60,000 is a key psychological level, and it came with little warning. Bitcoin price had held above $61,000 for most of the morning, even after a third straight daily loss. Stocks and rate hike bets drive the selloff Wall Street opened sharply lower. The Nasdaq Composite fell more than 2% in morning trading as shares of Anthropic extended losses in its second day since a record Nasdaq debut. Nvidia and AMD also traded lower. Bitcoin has been moving with tech stocks. The market has questioned whether heavy spending on artificial intelligence will pay off, and Friday’s open did nothing to ease that worry. Rate expectations are adding pressure. Traders see a roughly 94% chance the Federal Reserve raises rates in December, CME Group’s FedWatch tool showed . Higher rates tend to hurt bitcoin and other assets that pay no yield. Earlier Friday, South Korea’s Kospi index fell more than 5% and chipmakers sank across Asia. That selling carried into U.S. trading and then into bitcoin. Some analysts had flagged $60,000 as a floor. Katie Stockton of Fairlead Strategies told CNBC the bottom of bitcoin’s trading range sits “just below 60,000,” and that it “appears to be trying to find a footing.” Friday’s drop tests that view. CoinShares head of research James Butterfill said this week the drop is a “continuation of the existing bear market.” His base case is range trading around $60,000 to $90,000 through much of 2027. JUST IN: Bitcoin falls below $60,000 for the first time since June. BTC is now less than 4% away from a new cycle low pic.twitter.com/GSZkbGdzZz — Bitcoin Magazine (@BitcoinMagazine) November 20, 2026 ETF outflows and liquidations Funds have been sellers. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) lost $541.1 million on Thursday, its biggest one-day outflow on record. U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs lost about $582 million in total, extending a streak of heavy withdrawals this week. Leveraged traders were hit as well. More than $700 million in crypto positions were liquidated in the 24 hours before the latest drop, and about 86% were bets on higher prices. The slide below $60,000 likely forced out more of them. The move extends a month-long slump. Bitcoin has dropped roughly $20,000 in the past month, a slide tracked as the price fell under $62,000 on Thursday. item.title: Rutgers Football 2026 Opponent Q&A: Penn State
item.description: PISCATAWAY, NEW JERSEY - NOVEMBER 29: Kaytron Allen #13 of the Penn State Nittany Lions runs with the ball against the Rutgers Scarlet Knights during the first half at SHI Stadium on November 29, 2025 in Piscataway, New Jersey. (Photo by Ed Mulholland/Getty Images) | Getty Images Rutgers football is set to kick off against Penn State this Saturday at 3:30 pm in Happy Valley. Earlier this week, I had the opportunity to catch up with Brian Bennett of SB Nation’s Penn State site, blackshoediaries.com, to ask him about his thoughts on this game and the Nittany Lions season so far. 1. How has Matt Campbell adjusted to his new role in Happy Valley, and what does the fanbase think about this season so far? I think there’s been a learning curve for Campbell at Penn State. It’s just a different game playing in the Big Ten than in the Big XII when it comes to not only the talent on the field, but the expectations, media coverage, etc. He was super conservative in some early season games and it bit the Lions in home losses to Wisconsin and USC. Most on our staff looked at the schedule and thought this team should go at least 8-4/9-3. They still might get to 8-4, but there has certainly been some frustration. The schedule was light – Penn State didn’t play Oregon or Ohio State or Indiana. I think there was some hope that this team could follow the same template Curt Cignetti did at IU (bring over a bunch of guys familiar with the program, take advantage of an easy schedule, slide into the playoff and build some momentum). That was dashed when they blew a 17-point lead against Wisconsin. Then there were losses to Michigan and USC where the Lions led in the second half, too. 2. How has Rocco Becht adjusted over the course of his first season in the Big Ten? He’s been, for lack of a better term, “fine”. Becht was a hero in Ames. He’s just been a stopgap at Penn State. The Nittany Lions are 6-4, possibly on their way to 8-4, and there’s been no “Rocco moment” at all. In fact, he’s been the inverse of clutch. His three turnovers led to all three touchdowns for Michigan in a narrow loss in the Big House. Wisconsin’s rally was sparked by him missing a few throws and throwing a key interception. He hasn’t been good enough to elevate Penn State at any point in the year, but he’s also been solid in stretches where the team has been at its best – most notably in the first half at Washington. 3. What position battles will you be highlighting as the catalyst for this game? I will be watching Penn State’s defensive line and linebackers as they try to limit the Rutgers run game. I’ve seen Kirk Ciarrocca’s offense give Nittany Lion teams fits before (2019 when he was at Minnesota and certainly last year). That DL and linebacker crew is not exactly a strength of Penn State and Northwestern ran the ball all over them, while Michigan found success running it in the second half. item.title: Barcelona duo Ebrima Tunkara and Jordi Pesquer star as Spain’s Under-17s win World Cup opener
item.description: DOHA, QATAR - NOVEMBER 20: Ebrima Tunkara celebrates with Junior Zamorano of Spain after scoring his team’s second goal during the FIFA U-17 World Cup Qatar 2026 match between Spain and China PR at the Aspire Zone on November 20, 2026 in Doha, Qatar. (Photo by Lewis Storey - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images) | FIFA via Getty Images Barcelona starlets Ebrima Tunkara and Jordi Pesquer shone as Spain’s Under-17s won their first game of the World Cup campaign on Friday. Tunkara was named in the starting XI for the match against China alongside Pesquer and Barcelona team-mates Sergi Mayans and Roberto Tomás. ¡Este es nuestro primer 𝗢𝗡𝗖𝗘 del #U17WC ! 🇪🇸 – 🇨🇳 📺 @teledeporte y @rtveplay #NuestraBase pic.twitter.com/hVClsVzyv9 — Selección Española Masculina de Fútbol (@SEFutbol) November 20, 2026 Pesquer gave Spain the lead five minutes before half-time from the penalty spot. The left-back won the spot kick and dusted himself off to take it, sweeping the ball low and into the far corner to make it 1-0. Tunkara then doubled Spain’s lead in stoppage time at the end of the first half with a simply wonderful free-kick. The teenager guided the ball over the wall and past the dive of the goalkeeper to open his account for the tournament. GOOOOLAZO! Ebrima Tunkara scores with a great free-kick. 2-0 pic.twitter.com/rpwBKocx6G — ArsenKveFCB (@ArsenKveFCB) November 20, 2026 The Barcelona star was involved again as Spain made it 3-0 on 74 minutes. Tunkara shrugged off a couple of challenges inside his own half before powering forwards and laying the ball off to Owen Emeka out wide on the right. Emeka then drove into the area and fired the ball home from the angle to finish the game as a contest. Yet Spain were celebrating again five minutes later when Emeka grabbed his second of the match. Pesquer, who also enjoyed a great game, did well to get forward and fire a low shot goalwards. Jordi Pesquer’s shot leads to 4-0 for Spain U17. Sensational game by the young left-back. pic.twitter.com/g3bAnZoYoe — ArsenKveFCB (@ArsenKveFCB) November 20, 2026 China goalkeeper Jiang Yuhan could only parry the ball into Emeka’s path and the youngster had the simple task of tapping home from close range to make it 4-0. Spain wrapped up a great start with a fifth and final goal on 85 minutes which saw more Barcelona involvement. Substitute Iu Martinez fizzed in a delicious low cross from the right for Guillermo Trujillano to sweep home and seal an emphatic victory.

item.title: New Sheriff in Town: Michigan’s Whittingham on the Hot Seat?
item.description: Nov 14, 2026; Eugene, Oregon, USA; Michigan Wolverines head coach Kyle Whittingham watches the replay monitor during the second half in a game against the Oregon Ducks at Autzen Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Troy Wayrynen-Imagn Images Trev Alberts is heading to Ann Arbor at a difficult moment for Michigan football. The incoming athletic director inherits a program struggling through a 5-5 season , and first-year head coach Kyle Whittingham is already facing questions about whether he will get another year. Alberts, who is leaving Texas A&M to become Michigan’s next athletic director, is expected to begin his new role on Dec. 1. His appointment comes as the Wolverines try to recover from a disappointing season and a turbulent period for the athletic department. Bruce Feldman of The Athletic suggested the timing could be concerning for Whittingham. Speaking to Yahoo Sports, Feldman said that having a new athletic director in place before Thanksgiving is “probably bad news for Kyle Whittingham.” That comment reflects the growing uncertainty around the program, but Michigan has not announced any plans to replace its head coach. Michigan’s New Athletic Director Inherits a Difficult Situation Alberts replaces Warde Manuel , who announced in July that he would step down at the end of 2026. Manuel had served as Michigan’s athletic director since 2016, overseeing a period that included the football program’s national championship and several major controversies. The university moved quickly to secure Alberts, with incoming president C. Cybele Raver calling an emergency meeting of the Board of Regents to address the appointment. Alberts will have an opportunity to evaluate the athletic department as he takes over. His background includes athletic director roles at Nebraska and Texas A&M. At Nebraska, he made a major football decision in 2022, dismissing head coach Scott Frost midseason. Alberts subsequently hired Matt Rhule, who took over before the 2023 campaign. However, Alberts’ experience at Texas A&M offers an important distinction. He did not hire current Aggies head coach Mike Elko. Elko was already in place when Alberts arrived in College Station in March 2024. The new Michigan athletic director will have to determine whether Whittingham is the right person to lead the Wolverines forward. Whittingham Has Two Games to Change the Conversation Michigan’s record tells only part of the story. The Wolverines have lost five games, including defeats against Iowa, Minnesota, Michigan State, Oregon, and Indiana. Their offense has struggled to produce consistently, and Whittingham has already made a major staff change by dismissing offensive coordinator Jason Beck. The 31-7 loss to Oregon was particularly concerning. Michigan managed just seven points, continuing an offensive problem that has followed the team through much of the season. item.title: Filming training by drones should be illegal - Iraola
item.description: Andoni Iraola's Liverpool take on Mauricio Pochettino's Manchester United on Sunday [Getty Images] Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola says filming with drones around training grounds should be illegal after Mauricio Pochettino's first session as Manchester United boss was captured and uploaded online. Pochettino and his players were clearly visible in the footage, which was shot above United's Carrington training base from a variety of angles and distances. The drone operater apologised and later took down the footage, with sources telling BBC Sport they are adamant there was no security breach and that they do not intend to take legal action. Iraola said he was sent the 12 minutes of footage on Thursday - three days before United travel to Anfield for a Premier League match. "The important part of this is that it shouldn't be legal," he said on Friday. "It happened to United but it could happen to me. "Yesterday, when Sky Sports had access to our training and the cameras recorded 15-20 minutes, you know who trained and who didn't. "It's not the matter of the advantage. It's the fact that someone can do this. There's a reason we train behind closed doors because there are some things that you have to respect. I don't think it's nice for any club." Ten outfield players were seen working directly with former United States boss Pochettino in the footage, though it seems unlikely they will all start Sunday's match. "We've faced each other and obviously he [Pochettino] has a lot of Premier League games behind him that we can look at," said Iraola. "We can look at games from the US but it's true that they have this small advantage that we don't have references to prepare, because they can go different ways that we honestly don't know right now." Iraola said he expected United to be "well prepared" as Pochettino's assistants travelled to England to work with the players before the Argentine arrived on Wednesday. "They have this advantage that we don't exactly know - or at least we don't have the references like we do against other opposition," he said. "Especially the beginning of the game will be important. We have to adapt to certain things. But we know the players very well." Liverpool are fourth in the table - 14 places ahead of United. But they have failed to beat the Red Devils at Anfield in each of the past three seasons, and have lost to Arsenal and Manchester City at home already in this campaign. "You don't find bigger games than this," said Iraola. "I feel lucky to be here and privileged to be a part of these games. "We have to acknowledge the importance of the game. There are a lot of ingredients. They have a new manager, new challenges for us. This is important for us in a lot of different ways. "We want to improve our form at home. We have been very good away but not good at home and the first chance we have is United on Sunday." Pochettino training session filmed by drone - what did we learn? item.title: 'It is a matter of balance' - Enzo Maresca backs Gianluigi Donnarumma and Enzo Fernandez as Man City boss calls for calm ahead of Fulham clash
item.description: RB Leipzig v Manchester City - UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD4 - Getty Images Sport Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca has called for a sense of perspective as his side prepares to return to Premier League action against Fulham. Following a dip in results before the international break, the Italian tactician is determined to shield his high-profile stars from mounting external pressure. Finding stability amid the noise Reflecting on the recent run of results, Maresca emphasised the need for a measured approach, particularly after a spectacular start to his first Premier League season in charge of City, which saw him guide the team to a record seven consecutive wins - the best start to a managerial reign in the competition's history. However, City suffered three defeats in their following matches before the international break , which ends with Saturday's home clash against Fulham. 'I think there is always a reason why you win a game or you lose a game, no doubt. But it is a matter of balance,' Maresca explained. 'We were not perfect at the beginning when we were winning games and we've not been so bad when we lost the last three games. So that's why it is a matter of finding the right balance between the two things. And again, with the new players, a new manager, it is part of the process.' Maresca is well aware that even the most successful seasons are rarely without obstacles. He reminded supporters that adversity is a natural ingredient in the hunt for silverware. 'In all of the season when you achieve something important, you also go through difficult moments. I was here in the Treble season and we had some bad moments. It is normal and it is part of the season to drop some points, even more when you start something new like in our case with a new manager, new players and everything has changed.' Standing by Donnarumma Individual scrutiny has intensified during the break, particularly regarding Gianluigi Donnarumma. The Italian goalkeeper endured a challenging period with the national team in the UEFA Nations League, notably committing a high-profile error that allowed France to take the lead in Italy's 3-1 victory, before conceding four goals against Belgium. He has also made several costly mistakes for Manchester City during the 2026-27 season, including an error against Aston Villa that allowed Nicolas Jackson to score, leaving his near post exposed against RB Leipzig as Ridle Baku found the net from a tight angle, and facing criticism for his performance in City's 4-2 defeat to Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League. Maresca offered a full defence of his number one , acknowledging the errors while pointing to his shot-stopping qualities. 'He has been good,' Maresca said of Donnarumma. 'I think with the international team, he made a mistake in the build-up. But in Italy he was the man of the match in the game, he made many good saves. We made some mistakes in the last games. Gigi was part of that. He is aware. Hopeful

item.title: Maresca says struggling Man City not distracted by 'noise' around club
item.description: Enzo Maresca's Manchester City have lost their past three Premier League matches (Darren Staples) Enzo Maresca insists his Manchester City players are not distracted by the "noise" around the club's financial-rules case as he seeks to end their losing run. City flew out of the blocks in the Premier League this season, winning their first seven games, but three straight defeats have left them six points behind leaders Arsenal. The 10-time English champions are still waiting to discover the extent of their punishment after being found guilty of more than 100 breaches of Premier League financial rules. The club have repeatedly denied wrongdoing and have appealed against the verdict. But Maresca said he did not believe the case was weighing on the minds of his third-placed team ahead of their match against Fulham at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday. "I don't think the players are thinking too much about that," he said, "If we want to relate the noise with the defeats, Villa away, I think we had so many chances... Brighton here, the keeper was the man of the match. "The Forest one (a 3-1 defeat), where Erling (Haaland) had the chance to (make it) 2-2. I don't think the players are focused on the noise." Maresca admitted his side needed to improve but said not everything was perfect even when they were winning. "Overall, we control the game almost every time," said the Italian. "There are moments when we don't control the game and it is a moment when we need to understand the reason why and to do better." The former Chelsea boss, who replaced Pep Guardiola in the close-season, pointed out that he had not been at City for long, stressing his focus is on the long term. "Probably you forget a little bit about the time we spent together," he said. "It is not a big time that we are together. That is why I can see that what we are working on every day is there. "This is a good thing, it is a nice feeling. Also, the work we are doing is helping the players to be better players and to be a better team. For me, it is just the beginning of something long." City can take heart from their eye-catching 20-game winning run against Fulham in all competitions. "I didn't know that it's 20 games, hopefully 21," said Maresca. "It's a long time and hopefully tomorrow we can continue winning games against them." jw/smg/pi

item.title: Everything Texans HC DeMeco Ryans said following Week 11 win vs. Colts
item.description: Here's everything Houston Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans said following Thursday night's 26-3 win over the Indianapolis Colts, including his thoughts on the play of C.J. Stroud , the return of David Montgomery and more. DeMeco Ryans opening statement : First and foremost, praise; happy to get the win. All glory and praise to our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. Thankful for this moment, for our guys, for our team to represent at home in the right way and come away with the win. Proud of the effort from everyone. It took everybody. Total team effort. So proud of the way the guys represented tonight . Question: On DE Will Anderson Jr. DeMeco Ryans: "Will has a significant impact on our team not only by the way he plays but just the way he leads. That's every day. What you see out there on game day is what you see every day, the intensity that he represents, he shows it in practice, he shows it in the meeting room. That's one of the best players I've been around. From the player and the man, couldn't find a better guy than him and happy for the season he's having, proud of the way he continues to work, remain relentless, represent the way we need to represent. He's having an outstanding year and good things are coming his way." Q: On finishing the game against the Indianapolis Colts Ryans: “It's fulfilling to finally see that happen. We've been in these games a ton where we were up at the halftime and come out in the second half or whatever that reason has been and not finish. So for them to actually see it and go do it. I think that it will bode well for them gaining a ton of confidence for showing themselves that they can do it. They went out, they did it and hopefully we can continue to ride that formula." Q: On CB Kamari Lassiter stepping up in the past few weeks Ryans: "For the past three weeks, Kamari has played really great football. He's just locked in, just being where he's supposed to be, playing with the right technique, playing proper leverage and he makes plays he's supposed to make. He just has to continue to do that. Don't put a ton of pressure on himself. Just go out, execute how he knows how to execute. Rep his play style, which we all love, and he'll make the plays. So happy for him to finally get that interception today." Q: On RB David Montgomery returning to the lineup Ryans: "Very happy for David and the role that he played for us. It's been a long road to recovery for him so proud of the work he did in the background, but what he showed today is what we want to do. Come out and run the football. It starts with the offensive line, the way they control the line of scrimmage and David's just making some really good runs. When the runs were stuffed, he was able to still turn out and get four or five-yard gains. Really proud of the effort he showed today and having him back is significant for us. We can continue to run the ball like that. It only helps our entire team." Q: On the first win at home this season Ryans: "First and foremos

item.title: The tale of the Wolves fans who did not return from a world cup to be shown
item.description: The documentary follows the adventures of a group of Wolves fans who went to the Mexico World Cup in 1986 and never came back to the UK [Gary Allen] A screening of a documentary about a group of Wolves fans who went to the 1986 World Cup in Mexico and did not return to the Black Country will take place at the club. The group decided not to return to their Stourbridge and Lye homes after attending the global football spectacular, embarking on new lives in the US instead. Gary Allen, who settled in Atlanta and who pitched the documentary, said "Wolves called us and said 'would you like to do the first screening in the UK at the Molineux? And of course all being Wolves fans we said 'we'd love to'." Lost Down Mexico Way will be shown at Molineux on Friday evening, just one part of reunion gatherings this week. The stars of the documentary are referred to by their nicknames. As well as Allen, known as Adder, it features Rabbithead (Garry Hardwicke), Batesy (Stuart Bates), Arnie (David Arnold) and Texas Steve (Steve Dawson). After the World Cup and a brief jaunt to Belize, the gang flew to Dallas, Texas. Gary Allen, known as Adder, said "before you know it, there's 40 years gone" [Gary Allen] The group had lived in the Black Country all their lives before flying 5,000 miles to experience the 1986 tournament. Allen, who retired from running his own company last year, has previously said the "opportunity was the biggest thing for us", as he talked about the US. "I think back in 86... the job situation wasn't the best back then. "I'd just lost my job, [Margaret] Thatcher was in power, a few of the lads were just doing painting and whatever. "We'd all saved a bit of money and the idea was to go out there and do a few weeks and just travel. We just played it by ear really." Allen added once "we got there and enjoyed it, it just went from there and we all stayed and then more and more came over". "And before you know it, there's 40 years gone," he said. "So it was just a chance we took back in the day and luckily it's panned out well for us." Of those attending, a coach from Stourbridge was leaving on Friday afternoon "and about four or five carloads". "So we've got 80 [in] total that Wolves have given us tickets for, so it should be a good reunion," Allen added. Allen said he was looking forward to having a "good chat, good reminisce". "As you get older you can't do it. "So this is a one-off and it'll be the last time I see a lot of people, but it's gonna be great and we'll certainly make the most of it." Follow BBC Wolverhampton & Black Country on BBC Sounds , Facebook , X and Instagram . More on this story 'Emotional' World Cup reunion for expats who made Mexico home in '86 The football fans who went to a World Cup and loved it so much, they stayed Kevin Bridges explores state of football in 'heartfelt' World Cup documentary Related internet links Lost Down Mexico Way

item.title: Report Milan ready to sell Estupinan and Loftus-Cheek, loan young talent out
item.description: Report Milan ready to sell Estupinan and Loftus-Cheek, loan young talent out Milan are expected to sell Pervis Estupinan and Ruben Loftus-Cheek in the January transfer window, with Turkish and English clubs interested, while Francesco Camarda and Christian Comotto are heading on loan. The Rossoneri have stuttered so far this season and found significant differences between the first choice team’s performance and those who come in during squad rotation. This has prompted three defeats out of four Europa League games so far, and coach Ruben Amorim is reportedly ready to cut some players loose. Milan clear out dead wood JAKARTA, INDONESIA – AUGUST 08: Pervis Estupinan of AC Milan controls the ball against Pedro Neto of Chelsea FC during the pre-season friendly between Chelsea FC and AC Milan at Gelora Bung Karno Stadium on August 08, 2026 in Jakarta, Indonesia. (Photo by Peksi Cahyo/Getty Images) Amorim had declared at the start of the season that he convinced Milan to keep hold of Estupinan when a move to Aston Villa had been practically agreed. Now several months on, he seemingly regrets that decision and has given the all-clear for an exit, but the Premier League side is no longer interested. A loan move to Fiorentina could be on the cards , although they hope to find a more permanent solution to make back some of that investment. ITALY – SEPTEMBER 14: Ruben Loftus-Cheek of AC Milan in action during the Serie A match between AC Milan and Bologna FC 1909 at Giuseppe Meazza Stadium on September 14, 2025 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Loftus-Cheek is only under contract with the Rossoneri until the end of this season, but persistent injuries and poor performances should see him sold in January. Coventry City had made an approach in the summer, and could well try again, but Besiktas and other Turkish teams are also options. Francesco Camarda scores from the penalty spot during a pre-season friendly between Celtic and Milan at Celtic Park (via www.acmilan.com) Meanwhile, young players Camarda and Comotto are clearly not going to get a chance to deliver, so will be sent out on loan in January to gain valuable experience. Genoa are the most advanced in talks for midfielder Comotto, while Camarda has numerous proposals from Serie A, B, and even abroad.

item.title: Pochettino outlines his expectations in first Man Utd press conference
item.description: FILE PHOTO - USA manager and new Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino during press conference at the Arthur M. Blank National Training Centre. Pochettino has been appointed as Manchester United head coach from November 18, the club have announced. (is associated with: «Pochettino outlines his expectations in first Man Utd press conference») Press Association/PA Wire/dpa Mauricio Pochettino wants a say in “all the main decisions” around Manchester United’s squad after arriving as the club’s new head coach this week. Pochettino addressed the media for the first time as United boss on Friday, two days before the trip to face old rivals Liverpool – a match United will start inside the relegation zone. United’s recent recruitment has come in for heavy criticism with a feeling that Pochettino’s predecessor Michael Carrick was left short-handed by the club’s summer business, overseen by director of football Jason Wilcox. While he has accepted the title of head coach, former Tottenham and Chelsea boss Pochettino made clear he wants to have a big say behind the scenes. “Since I started at Espanyol, head coach, coach, manager…in the end it’s not changing too much, because I think the way that we work is indifferent to the title description,” Pochettino said. “Sometimes I worked much better when I was head coach or when I was coach than manager, and it’s not necessarily that if you are manager you have all the decisions. Maybe you are a coach and have more power in the decision. “It depends on the structure, depends on the communication, depends on the relationship with all the areas. I know that being a head coach I am the guy that is going to decide the squad for Sunday, I’m going to pick the starting 11 and make the changes. “Of course in the future I would like to be involved in all the main decisions that will happen on the squad. In the end Manchester United is a football club.” One decision Pochettino has already made is that Bruno Fernandes will remain as club captain. The 32-year-old, who was outspoken in his comments towards the end of Carrick’s tenure and has struggled to replicate last season’s form, is out of contract in the summer, although the club have an option for another 12 months. “Bruno is our captain and I think a very important player but all the players have to feel they are important from the bottom to the top,” Pochettino said. “Yesterday we spent three hours chatting individually in my office with all the players. Maybe I missed some injured players but in the next few days we will have time to talk in an individual way with everyone. “I think it’s important to listen to what they need to say, to understand the place they are in, not only on the field but off it and what is going on… “But Bruno is our captain and he’s a very important player.” Pochettino is the latest big name United have turned to in a bid to get back to the top of the English game, seeking to succeed where the likes of José Mourinho, Louis van Gaal, Eri

item.title: Alcaraz concerned over fitness despite win over Cobolli at ATP Finals
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Team Europe's Carlos Alcaraz in action against Team World's Taylor Fritz during the men's singles group stage match on day two of the Laver Cup tennis tournament at The O2. (is associated with: «Alcaraz concerned over fitness despite win over Cobolli at ATP Finals») Adam Davy/PA Wire/dpa Carlos Alcaraz remains concerned about his fitness despite a straightforward victory over Flavio Cobolli at the ATP Finals. The Spaniard extended his winning run to 12 matches with his third straight-sets win in Turin, seeing off Italian Cobolli 6-4, 6-1. Alcaraz, who had already booked his spot in the last four, arrived in Italy with concerns over a right knee niggle and took a medical timeout to have his left hamstring strapped during a victory over Daniil Medvedev on Wednesday. There had been speculation he might pull out and, although he appears in great form, Alcaraz admitted his physical struggles are a worry. He said on atptour.com: “The challenge is no longer on the court, it is off the court, to do whatever it takes to be physically ready for the match tomorrow. It is going to be a really important next day.” Alcaraz is scheduled to take on Ben Shelton in the last four on Saturday. Britain’s Neal Skupski and his American partner Christian Harrison booked their spot in the doubles semi-finals with a 7-6 (7-5), 6-4 victory over third seeds Marcel Granollers and Horacio Zeballos. Meanwhile, ATP Tour chair Andrea Gaudenzi defended his absence from the ceremony earlier this week honouring world number one doubles pair Henry Patten and Harri Heliovaara. Gaudenzi was present during a similar ceremony for singles number one Alexander Zverev and Patten publicly criticized his decision not to attend. The row comes against the backdrop of controversial plans to reduce prize money and opportunity for doubles players on the men’s tour, of which Patten has been a leading critic. Gaudenzi told a press conference that the ceremony had clashed with an important meeting, saying: “I can guarantee it was not done intentionally to deliver a message. Not at all. We wouldn’t be that silly, because we know that the situation is tense now. “I have had a meeting with Harri and the working group of doubles in Paris for hours until 8pm. I understand it’s emotional for them. I feel the pain for them.” Gaudenzi added that there is not yet consensus on the proposals, with further discussions planned for next month.

item.title: Manchester United travel to Anfield with 'advantage' claims Andoni Iraola despite drone footage
item.description: Andoni Iraola's Liverpool will host Manchester United on Sunday -Credit:Gaspafotos/MB Media, Getty Images Andoni Iraola has argued that it is Liverpool who will be at a disadvantage when they face Manchester United at Anfield on Sunday. United head into the weekend sitting 18th in the Premier League table with just one win from their opening 10 matches. The fixture will mark Mauricio Pochettino's first game at the helm since arriving from his previous role in the United States on Wednesday. Pochettino faces an enormous challenge in turning around his underperforming squad, and his preparations were further complicated when a rogue drone operator filmed his first training session on Thursday and posted the footage to YouTube. The 12-minute clip has since been removed , but appeared to expose details of Pochettino's tactical preparations on the training ground. Mauricio Pochettino took charge of his first training session with Manchester United on Thursday -Credit:Ash Donelon, Manchester United via Getty Images Iraola acknowledged that he had been sent the video and, while expressing sympathy for Pochettino, dismissed the notion that United had been placed at a disadvantage by the drone incident. "They sent me yesterday the footage," Iraola said in his pre-match press conference via The Mirror . "But I think the important part is that it shouldn't be legal. It happened to United but it could happen today to me in training you know. "Yesterday you had access to our training, the cameras in the corridors for 15 or 20 minutes, I don't know how much. You know who's training with us, who didn't train. We know the same (with United). "But it's not [about] the matter of the advantage, it's about the fact that someone can do this... I think there's a reason we train behind closed doors because there are some things that you have to respect and I don't think it's nice for any club, honestly." Iraola also believes that because Pochettino is beginning with a blank canvas at United, his Liverpool scouting team have been unable to prepare in their usual manner. To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE When asked about his familiarity with Pochettino, Iraola responded: "We've faced each other and obviously he has lots of Premier League games behind him that we can look at. "We can look at games from the U.S., but it's true that they have this small advantage that we don't have references to prepare. They can go different ways and, honestly, we don't know right now." United have opted against pursuing legal action against the drone operator, who issued a grovelling apology on Friday morning. A statement read: "I would like to speak about yesterday's incident. A total error of judgement on my part led to me filming some of the Manchester United training session at Carrington, whilst the flight was legal in terms of drone laws I fully accept it was unethical on my part. item.title: 3 Yankees starting pitchers who should move to the bullpen
item.description: 3 Yankees starting pitchers who should move to the bullpen originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New York Yankees have a surplus of starting pitchers and only five spots in the rotation. Cam Schlittler, Max Fried, Gerrit Cole, Carlos Rodon, and Will Warren round out the top five. Ryan Weathers is also a candidate for the rotation's final spot. Or, Weathers could transition to the bullpen after throwing a career-high 137.1 innings in 2026. Several other pitchers in New York's system can start games, but there's not enough room for everyone. If none of these players are traded this offseason, here are the internal bullpen options the Yankees should consider. Clarke Schmidt Schmidt's first full season (2022) in the Majors was spent as a reliever, and he posted a 3.12 ERA in 57.2 innings. He finally returned from Tommy John Surgery in September but landed on the IL again after just one appearance. The right-hander missed the postseason with right biceps neuritis. Simply, there's no longer space for Schmidt in the rotation with Weathers and Warren's emergence. It's fair to say that both pitchers are ahead of him on the depth chart. Still, Schmidt can be a valuable multi-inning guy for Aaron Boone. Elmer Rodriguez Considering he has minor league options, the Yankees would be wise to keep Rodriguez as rotation depth at Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre if multiple injuries occur. Or, they could give him a chance to make an impact in the Majors, using him as a reliever who can provide length. MORE : Phillies sign ex-Pirates, Yankees veteran reliever with 4.82 ERA in 2026 Rodriguez posted a 5.40 ERA and 1.57 WHIP with an elevated 12.8% walk rate in six starts in 2026, but he showed flashes of what made him a top prospect. Carlos Lagrange Lagrange has spent most of his minor league career as a starter, but the Yankees hoped to use him in the bullpen as a late-season call-up before a shoulder injury. That should be the plan for him again, at least until a spot in the rotation opens up. The 23-year-old, who often tops 100 mph with his fastball, struck out 85 batters in 64.1 innings this past season at Triple-A. Lagrange must improve his command (11.2 BB%) to be effective in high-leverage innings, but there's a lot to be excited about as he looks to make his Major League debut in 2027. item.title: Latest Drake Maye Injury Update Spells Bad News for Patriots' Playoff Hopes
item.description: Latest Drake Maye Injury Update Spells Bad News for Patriots' Playoff Hopes originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Nearly one week after Drake Maye was knocked out of the Patriots ' Week 10 clash against the Lions with an ankle injury, there remains a paucity of details over just how long the third-year passer will be out of commission. Multiple reporters, including ESPN's Adam Schefter , tipped Maye with missing most — if not all — of the season with "some type of fracture in his ankle." New England hasn't been nearly as declarative, offering precious few details outside of forecasting that Maye will miss the Patriots' next game, a Week 12 tilt against the Chargers. A recent report adds to the growing chorus of voices suggesting that Maye is unlikely to play in another Patriots game this season. Here's what you need to know. MORE: A.J. Brown's Latest Injury Leaves Patriots Facing Uncomfortable Questions Latest Drake Maye Injury Update is Bad News for Patriots' Playoff Hopes New England hasn't yet to provide a full scope of Maye's injury. The Patriots sidewinder has a fractured ankle, according to multiple reports. But the severity of that malady — and the timeline for his return — has been cloaked in uncertainty. The Ringer's Tom Pelissero says the Patriots' obsfucation has been intentional. Appearing on "The Bill Simmons Podcast", Pelissero offered some insight into why New England has yet to give a straight answer on whether Maye will miss the remainder of the season. "It's the Patriots and they have a history of doing these things with injuries," Pelissero said. Pelissero confirmed that Maye is back in the United States and he did suffer a fracture in his ankle. He spurned offering details on the nature of Maye's fracture but, according to his estimation, it seems unlikely that he'll be back this season. "I would be surprised if we see Drake Maye again this season," Pelissero said. "Even if they go to the playoffs, I don't foresee Drake Maye being back based upon what I know right now." Pelissero said that he's assuming Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel will give more concrete details about Maye's injury when New England comes out of the bye week. He also surmised that the Patriots will give the reins to Tommy DeVito fully in Maye's absence, pouring cold water on the suggestion that the Pats could take a look at former hurler Jimmy Garoppolo, who hasn't thrown a pass since 2024. "I don't know if Jimmy Garoppolo straight off the couch is better than Tommy DeVito," Pelissero queried. Withouts its talisman, the Patriots offense looks a lot less toothless. On a literal basis, New England remains in the thick of the hunt for a wild-card spot. DeVito performed decently enough in relief of Daniel Jones during the 2023 season with the Giants. Still, the road towards postseason contention looks an onerous one for Vrabel's side, especially with matchups against the Bills, Chiefs, Vikings and Broncos still remainin

item.title: Rory McIlroy attends first NHL game, fires up Maple Leafs locker room
item.description: Rory McIlroy has experienced his share of firsts in his day, including finally slipping on the green jacket at Augusta National. On Thursday night, the 37-year-old added another, albeit slightly less historic, item to the list. McIlroy attended his first NHL game, taking in the Toronto Maple Leafs ' matchup against the Los Angeles Kings at Scotiabank Arena. And he wasn't exactly an anonymous fan in the crowd. Before the puck dropped, McIlroy went inside the Maple Leafs' locker room and read Toronto's starting lineup to the players. The team later shared video of the moment on social media. McIlroy also spent some time with Carlton the Bear, the Leafs' mascot, before eventually settling into a suite for the game. Cameras caught McIlroy watching the action, which naturally brought back a prediction he made in Toronto about a year earlier. At the 2025 RBC Canadian Open , two months after winning his first Masters title, McIlroy was presented with a Maple Leafs jersey by team CEO (and former DP World Tour CEO) Keith Pelley. That's when McIlroy offered Toronto fans a little hope. "If I can win the Masters, then the Leafs can win the Stanley Cup," McIlroy said at the time. McIlroy has since won another Masters, capturing his second green jacket in April, so perhaps the pressure is officially on Toronto. Maple Leafs coach Jim Hiller certainly didn't mind having one of golf's biggest stars around the team. "What an honor for us to have him," Hiller said. "We got a chance to meet with him a little bit as coaches and then the players. If you are wondering what an athlete, a pro, a winner and all the things, you can add all the superlatives you want, that's him. "He's gone through some difficult times at certain times too and he just powered through so I think he's just a great example for us right here right now." Take it away, @McIlroyRory 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/ITE1P0Dnw8 — Toronto Maple Leafs (@MapleLeafs) November 20, 2026 The Leafs lost the game in overtime and are currently tied for last place in the Atlantic Division. This moment was a high after what McIlroy revealed just days earlier in Dubai. McIlroy became emotional after securing a record-tying eighth Race to Dubai title at the season-ending DP World Championship, matching Colin Montgomerie's eight European Tour Order of Merit crowns. During his post-round interview, McIlroy revealed his father had spent nearly two months in the hospital after undergoing major surgery at the end of September. "He's been in the hospital for the last two months. He underwent a huge operation at the end of September, and he's recovering well, thankfully," McIlroy said. McIlroy stopped, covered his eyes with his hands and took a moment to compose himself. "This one's for him." McIlroy said he visited his father in Cleveland before traveling to Dubai for the DP World Championship. Before he left, his father had a simple message for him: "Go win the Race to Dubai." item.title: Geno Auriemma’s salary has got everyone talking after his NIL comments
item.description: Photo by Chris Carter/Getty Images UConn head coach Geno Auriemma found himself at the center of a heated online debate. Geno Auriemma has spent over four decades turning UConn into the gold standard of college basketball. Since taking the job in 1985, he’s become the winningest coach in NCAA history, men’s or women’s, piling up 12 national titles, 25 Final Fours, and six undefeated seasons. Now in his 42nd year on the sideline, his Huskies are sitting at 3–2 after navigating a brutal early slate, taking tough road losses to ranked Michigan and Louisville squads. Geno Auriemma criticises new college wages Speaking candidly about the current state of high school recruiting and NIL deals, Geno Auriemma didn’t mince words about million-dollar price tags and what recruits are really chasing. He said: “I just don’t see the value of paying a high school kid a million dollars to come out of high school that hasn’t dribbled the ball one time in college…That’s more than 90% of best players in the world in the WNBA. “We have an agent that talks to their agent because the kids and the parents lie to you. ‘It’s not about the money. It’s about academics. It’s about finding the right fit. It’s about the right experience.’ No it isn’t. Just say it’s about the money, and we can all live happily ever after.” This sparked a debate over Auriemma’s salary, which makes for interesting reading. One fan said: “$3.5M: Geno’s annual salary. $1.2M: Highest WNBA HC annual salary but always wanna talk about player $$$.” “He’s earned it. Which WNBA coach has 12 championships?” This fan defended Auriemma. Another joined in: “With his resume, he is grossly underpaid…” “There is NO high school player worth $1M.” This supporter said. Lastly, this fan made a valid point: “Geno’s been coaching at UConn since 1985 and has brought the program over 1500 wins, 12 national championships and six of the ten undefeated seasons in women’s college basketball ever.” Auriemma’s own paycheck actually makes the gap look even wider. He signed a five-year, $18.7 million extension at UConn in 2024, good for around $3.74 million a season, which comfortably clears even the highest-paid WNBA head coaches, whose salaries generally top out between $1 million and $1.5 million. item.description: SAN JOSE, CALIFORNIA - NOVEMBER 11: Sidney Crosby #87 of the Pittsburgh Penguins shoots the puck while defended by Michael Kesselring #7 of the San Jose Sharks during the third period of an NHL hockey game at SAP Center on November 11, 2026 in San Jose, California. Vásquez/Getty Images) | Getty Images Pat Brisson issued a statement yesterday, on the heels of Penguins general manager Kyle Dubas holding a press conference Wednesday w here he indicated trades could soon be made with a “future-oriented” tilt for the team to get young player and prospects in the door while sending veterans out. Names like Rickard Rakell and Erik Karlsson are swarming fast in the rumor mill. Had Bryan Rust not been injured, he’d be right there with them. All three of those players are usually on the ice with 39-year old Sidney Crosby. When uninjured, all three are usually in the top-5 of scoring on the team. Dubas’ message was clear that the next phase of team-building is on the way and it’s going to be to stock the deck with youth. In the modern era, one has to wonder how camp Crosby would respond to that, especially since it wasn’t that long ago that Brisson made no secret that, “we want Sidney to hopefully be in the playoffs every year. We want him to hopefully win another Cup or two”. Pens GM Kyle Dubas told media Wednesday that it will be up to Sidney Crosby what he wants to do as far as his future, a respectful stance he has maintained on the iconic captain. Here’s a statement from Crosby’s agent Pat Brisson today on the matter: “Sidney has been in Pittsburgh for over 20 years and he isn’t in any rush to make a decision. Kyle will do what he feels is best for the organization in the meantime.” If this was a game of ‘big deal, little deal, no deal’, in a sense the whole turn of events for the week is a very big deal. In a sense, the Penguins have been in a form of a reset/rebuild (whatever form you want to use) since the Jake Guentzel trade. However, they have not steered hard into that direction, keeping around several veterans and still trying to see out the Crosby/Evgeni Malkin era for its natural time. Those decisions, plus a bunch of fortunate outcomes from other moves, worked out well and enabled the Penguins to be in a spot to make the playoffs last year. The recipe didn’t come together as cleanly for this season, and the team is ending the era on their own by dropping to the bottom of the division, conference and NHL at-large through the first 21 games of the season. item.description: Thomas Shea-Imagn Images Texans’ CJ Stroud didn’t want to lie about how he’s feeling after cooking Colts appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . CJ Stroud played it off when Will Anderson Jr. showered him with praise during the postgame interview after the Houston Texans walloped the Indianapolis Colts, 26-3, at Reliant Stadium on Thursday. It was a modest move. But really, Stroud should have flexed. He was brilliant against the Colts, throwing 21-of-27 for 194 yards and three touchdowns. He also had six carries for 27 yards. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) In a report from ESPN’s DJ Bien-Aime, the 25-year-old quarterback was not as shy. He opened up about his self-belief , which has helped the Texans win four of their last six games to stay in the hunt for a spot in the playoffs. “I knew what type of player I could be in this league, and to just get in that groove and have a rhythm, it’s been amazing. Honestly, I would be lying to you if I said it didn’t feel good,” said Stroud. He also became introspective as he acknowledged his privilege and professed his faith. “I’m very grateful for this opportunity to even play in the NFL. People probably think I’m crazy for always saying that, but I really did not expect my life to be like this. It’s nothing but the grace of God that I’m sitting up here and playing the way that I am,” added the one-time Pro Bowler. Bien-Aime noted that the Texans are looking to become the second team in league history to reach the playoffs after a 0-4 start. The San Diego Chargers did it in 1992. Houston’s odds of making the playoffs increased by 23% after crushing Indianapolis, which failed to score a touchdown for the first time since 2024. The Texans will go as far as Stroud will take them. But in the meantime, Stroud would like to cherish the win against the Colts. item.title: The Pacers Are Looking For Help: 5 Under-The-Radar Players Who Could Make A Difference
item.description: Nov 13, 2026; Indianapolis, Indiana, USA; Indiana Pacers forward Pascal Siakam (43) celebrates with guard Aaron Nesmith (23) in the second half against the New York Knicks at Gainbridge Fieldhouse. Mandatory Credit: Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images The Indiana Pacers are having some bad luck this season, and it’s hard to see things getting better soon. After making the NBA Finals in 2025, they lost Tyrese Haliburton to a torn Achilles, played the whole 2025-26 season without him, and finished with a 19-63 record. They were hoping to have him back this year, but he only played four games before hurting his left hamstring after a stellar return with 21.8 points and 9.5 assists. Now the Pacers are 5-10, and they just lost 119-104 to the Rockets last night, sitting 10th in the East. So yeah, they need some help, and it looks like they’re already trying to find it. Jake Fischer reported that the Pacers have been looking at possible trades for players who wouldn’t cost too much. They were also interested in Nique Clifford before the Kings traded him to the Thunder , so Indiana is definitely looking at what could be available on the market. And I think they should make a move. They still have Pascal Siakam , Andrew Nembhard, and Haliburton when he comes back, but the team around them needs more help. They could use another shooter, someone who can defend, or just a player who can give them 20 good minutes every game. Nothing too crazy, and they don’t have to trade all their picks for that. There are a few players around the league who could help the Pacers without costing a lot, so let’s look at five names they should consider. 1. A.J. Green As A Top Shooter Indiana Pacers Receive: A.J. Green Milwaukee Bucks Receive: Jarace Walker, 2028 first-round pick (lottery-protected) The Pacers need shooting, and A.J. Green could be a good option without making a huge trade. He’s putting up 5.9 points, 1.3 rebounds, and 1.3 assists this season, shooting 41.9% from three. Those aren’t crazy numbers, but he’s playing only 16.3 minutes per game, and his shooting could help Indiana a lot. Green is making $10.0 million this season and has three more years on his contract after this one. That’s a good deal for a player who can shoot like him, especially for a Pacers team that needs more players who can hit open threes when Haliburton comes back. The Bucks are already 1-15, so I think they should at least think about getting younger players and picks. Jarace Walker is only 23 and has struggled with Indiana, putting up 6.1 points, 5.1 rebounds, and 1.6 assists on 33.3% from the field. Maybe a new team could help him, and Milwaukee would also get a protected first-round pick for its rebuild. I like this trade for the Pacers, but giving up a first-round pick for Green might be a little too much. It would depend on how much they want him. 2. item.title: View From The Other Offseason – Ivan the Great of Battery Power
item.description: In 2025, the Braves finally seemed to right themselves after a couple of shaky years, winning their division despite a rash of injuries, especially to their starting pitching. However, even after winning their seventh division title in ten years, they ran into the Dodgers who managed to shutdown their bats and knock them out of the postseason in the NLDS 3-1. We talked to Ivan the Great of Battery Power about their takeaways from the 2026 season and what the Braves can look forward to in 2027. With the 2026 season in the rearview mirror, what do team fans think are the key takeaways, both good and bad on the season? I think this is one of those things where asking five Braves fans will give you seven opinions. On top of that, the Braves had a very strange 2026 season, which only makes the narrative more complicated. The good is that the Braves ended up where they were expected to be: lots of wins, on top of the division. There’s still clearly a fair bit of talent in the organization, and there are things the organization does really well, namely in major league pitching development. The bad is that 2026 was Year Two of “some component of the organization has no idea what to do offensively.” After a very specific offensive approach that we jokingly call “The PowerPoint” from 2019-2024, the Braves pivoted away from it hard in 2025 to disastrous results – and 2026 was a mixed bag of stuff that sometimes looked like 2019-2024, sometimes looked like 2025, and often just felt like flailing for a life preserver. Combine that with blow after blow of pitching injuries, and I think I’d probably list the takeaways as: 1) the team has a lot of good players; 2) the organization is for some reason unsure or incapable of getting the most out of those players on the hitting end; and, 3) the pitching health is always more dire than the organization seems to plan for, such that it’s an ongoing scramble for more arms that feels a bit like juggling chainsaws. What would you consider the team front office’s priority to be this offseason (assuming we’ll have baseball like normal next year)? I think broadly, and from a “fill the depth chart” perspective, it’s probably “actually find enough pitching that the chainsaws don’t all fall on your head.” But, things I’ve heard have leaned more towards, “we really gotta figure out the whole offense thing.” It kind of makes sense: the organization has done well with getting guys like Tyler Mahle and Martin Perez to not only not kill the team, but be fine-to-good, and Chris Sale somehow found another gear in his late 30s. But the hitting is… who can say, really. The Front Office seems caught between the personnel acquired and extended during the PowerPoint era and a pivot to a proto-Brewers walks-and-liners, though they’re nowhere near succeeding in the latter. Figuring out what they’re actually going to do offensively, both in terms of which personnel they add for shortstop and left field, and in terms of what they’re gonna work

item.title: Wilder confirms Sheffield United star is facing a year out following operation
item.description: Wilder confirms Sheffield United star is facing a year out following operation Sheffield United boss Chris Wilder has confirmed Femi Seriki is expected to be sidelined for around a year after suffering a ruptured patella tendon. The young wing-back sustained the serious injury just six minutes after coming on against Charlton Athletic and has since undergone surgery. “He’s had an operation. He’s going to be out for 12 months,” Wilder said. “You know, straight away. I think we all knew where that was going. How he awkwardly landed, and straight away, I think you always go on the reaction of the players. “It’s a testing time for him and a testing time for us because we’re losing a really attack-minded player that we were looking forward to getting back amongst us. “He was finding his feet. He was coming off the bench, and he probably would have been in contention to start now, but that’s not the case. I’m gonna have to get on with it.” Wilder also provided an update on Ryan One, who is likely to remain unavailable until the start of 2027 after suffering a setback in training. “He’s about a month or six weeks away,” Wilder said. “So, I think the start of 2027, he’ll be back. We’re going to have to take a little bit more time with him.”

item.title: Isaac TeSlaa Reveals Jared Goff Nearly Cost Him Priceless Detroit Lions Souvenir
item.description: Detroit Lions wide receiver Isaac TeSlaa waited all season to score his first touchdown of 2026, and when it finally happened against the New England Patriots in Germany, he was understandably fired up. Unfortunately, his excitement nearly cost him a souvenir he desperately wanted to keep. During an exclusive sit-down interview with Brad Galli on The Brad Galli Show , TeSlaa revealed the hilarious story of how quarterback Jared Goff accidentally sent his touchdown football into the crowd during Detroit’s 35-10 victory over New England in Munich. And for a little while, TeSlaa thought his football was gone forever. Detroit Lions wide receiver Isaac TeSlaa (18), center, celebrates a touchdown against New England Patriots with wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown (14), left, and running back Jahmyr Gibbs (0) during the first half at Allianz Arena in Munich, Germany on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Jared Goff Accidentally Sends Isaac TeSlaa’s Touchdown Ball Into Crowd TeSlaa scored on a spectacular 12-yard touchdown reception from Goff during the second quarter of Sunday’s victory. The play gave Detroit a 14-3 lead and marked TeSlaa’s first touchdown of the season. Normally, the Lions receiver makes a point of hanging on to footballs from his touchdowns. However, the excitement of scoring in Germany caused him to forget his usual routine. “Obviously, I scored the touchdown, and most of the time I try to hang on to the ball because I like keeping the game balls. But I was just too fired up,” TeSlaa told Galli. After making the catch, TeSlaa spiked the football in celebration and assumed someone would retrieve it. That’s when things took an unexpected turn. According to TeSlaa, one of Detroit’s ball boys was heading over to collect the football when Goff picked it up and threw it toward his father in the stands. There was just one problem. Goff wasn’t sure his dad actually caught it. TeSlaa didn’t learn what happened until he returned to the sideline and a teammate told him that Goff had thrown his football into the crowd. Initially, he thought the teammate was joking. But after speaking directly with Goff, he realized the situation was legitimate. “So I’m sitting there. I’m like, ‘This is my first touchdown of the season, and I’m in Germany. How many opportunities to score in Germany, and I don’t have my ball?'” Not exactly the souvenir situation TeSlaa had envisioned. TeSlaa Gets His Football Back, But Has One Question Fortunately, the story took another unexpected turn when TeSlaa returned to the Lions’ facility on Tuesday. After enjoying the team’s Monday off, he walked into the locker room and discovered that his touchdown football had apparently been returned. “Monday’s off. We get some time to sleep in, get the body back, and then I come in on Tuesday, and the game ball’s just sitting there in my locker,” TeSlaa explained. Problem solved, right? Well, not quite. item.title: Quarterly Business Report: New Jersey Devils
item.description: NEWARK, NEW JERSEY - NOVEMBER 18: Arseny Gritsyuk #81 of the New Jersey Devils warms up before the NHL game against the against the Montreal Canadiens at Prudential Center on November 18, 2026 in Newark, New Jersey. (Photo by Andrew Mordzynski/Getty Images) | Getty Images ( That Grits picture is how I feel about the team right now. Also this was written pre-Montreal game and does not include those numbers ). We are officially 25% of the way through the season, so I decided to do a quarterly check in on the underlying process, sample size and all. It seems like a TON has happened since opening night against the Flyers, and well.. it has. We’ve laughed, we’ve cried, we got ourselves a goalie, its been a whirlwind. But, we have quickly put .500 in the rearview and if you trusted the process, you’ve been rewarded with a team at the top of a lot of analytic rankings, top 10 in the standings, is scoring, defending, and getting saves. We seem pretty good, right? However, as good as the process has been all season, they did have to clean some things up after sputtering a bit out of the gate. They were giving up some egregious chances against and weren’t getting any sort of timely saves. Couple that with early finishing problems and it’s a recipe for “same old Devils.” However, after the Detroit game they held a team meeting to discuss structural and commitment changes, and since they have been a swarming, dominant 60 minute team for the most part. The timely saves thing got fixed by adding Hellebuyck. I’d also emphasize that even with the trend line going up, there are still things this team needs to work on – and I think that’s a good thing. They were on their heels more at the end of this marathon stretch of 7 games in 12 days. Special teams are a serious pain point. Consistency has also been this team’s primary bugaboo for years and it has only been one month, so we will see if they can keep this up, but the ball has started rolling downhill, vibes are high and to quote/paraphrase Luke Hughes after Vegas: “We’re having fun, this is a fun group.” Overall Team Metrics Through the first 21 games of the season, the Devils are 2nd by points percentage in the metro with a .714 and 4th in the league at 16-5-0. That is a 120 point pace. At this point last year we were also sitting pretty well, 13-5-1 with a .711 points percentage and 2nd in the league. While in a similar position, this team feels different as last season was largely driven by smoke and mirrors as most of the 25-26 boxcar stats were middling at best: I used the Detroit game as a demarcation point, as that when they had a team meeting to button up their defensive play. They have been out right dominant in all three zones (even with a couple of clunkers in there) and their commitment to puck support, back tracking, and a stalwart defensive blueline has helped the results start matching the process numbers. You can almost see in real time the entire team buying into this process and how it leads

item.title: NWSL Championship preview: Trinity Rodman and Washington Spirit chase redemption as Croix Bethune and Kansas City Current eye first title
item.description: NWSL Finals Preview - GOAL The Current bring a seven-match winning streak to Saturday’s final at Audi Field. GOAL breaks down the key matchups and picks a winner. The Washington Spirit are back in the NWSL Championship for a third straight year. After losing the last two finals, they’ll get another shot at the title on home turf against the Kansas City Current, who are chasing their first championship with a former Spirit star in midfield. Croix Bethune led the league with 11 assists for Kansas City. Her former teammate Trinity Rodman has put together one of her best seasons for Washington, scoring 14 goals and adding 10 assists. The Spirit beat the Current 4-0 at Audi Field in April, but Kansas City has won three of the teams’ last five meetings. Ahead of Saturday’s final, GOAL breaks down how both teams got here, picks out the players and X-factors that could decide the title and offers score predictions. Kansas City Current The Kansas City Current are chasing their first-ever NWSL Championship. How they got there The Current enter the final on a seven-match winning streak, having outscored opponents 18-4 during that run. They beat Angel City FC 1-0 in the quarterfinals before knocking out Shield winners Gotham FC 2-1 in the semifinals. Haley Hopkins scored the winner against Gotham to send Kansas City to its second NWSL final and first since 2022. Key players Temwa Chawinga The two-time NWSL MVP has just one goal contribution in her last five games, but she remains Kansas City’s biggest individual threat. Her pace and strength mean one pass behind Washington’s back line can turn into a clear chance. Croix Bethune The 2026 NWSL Midfielder of the Year sets the tempo for Kansas City and creates chances through the middle. Against her former club, she’ll be the player the Current look to for a pass that splits Washington’s defense. X factor Haley Hopkins has scored 13 goals this season and has made the most of the space available to her in the playoffs. If the Spirit commit extra defenders to Chawinga, Hopkins can punish them for it. Biggest strength Kansas City scored a league-best 54 goals in the regular season. Debinha, Michelle Cooper, Bethune and Hopkins give the Current several ways to create and finish chances, even when opponents keep Chawinga quiet. Biggest weakness Kansas City’s biggest defensive test will come when they lose the ball with numbers forward. If Washington can find Trinity Rodman early, she can run at the Current’s back line before it has time to reset. Washington Spirit Washington Spirit have been in the NWSL Championship for the past consecutive two seasons. item.title: Asali Africa: Serves Up ‘There’s Rice at Home’ A New Cooking Series Hosted by Chef Soliat Bada
item.description: Chef Soliat Bada Anyone who grew up in a Nigerian home knows the line. You suggest buying food outside, and before you finish the sentence, someone reminds you that there’s rice at home. It is usually the end of the conversation. In Asali Africa’s new series, it is where the conversation starts. There’s Rice at Home is a cooking and conversation show from Asali Africa, the Lagos-based creative development agency, hosted by Chef Soliat Bada . In each episode, Soliat cooks one rice dish with a guest, and while the pot does its work, the two get into the kind of talk that usually happens around food: family, money and what success really looks like. Rice is the most ordinary thing in a Nigerian kitchen, and the show makes a good case that it doesn’t have to taste ordinary. Over five episodes, released every two weeks, the menu travels from Jamaica to Saudi Arabia, back home to Nigeria and on to Louisiana. You don’t just watch the food get made, either. The recipes are written up in full on Asali Africa’s website, with the ingredients and method laid out step by step, so you can watch Soliat cook a dish and then make it in your own kitchen. The season opens with Rice and Peas with Oxtail, the Jamaican Sunday staple of rice cooked in coconut milk with red kidney beans (the “peas”), served beside rich, slow-cooked oxtail. Soliat’s guest is Michael Famoroti , co-founder of Stears, and their conversation turns to family and black tax: the expectation that once you start earning, you start supporting the people who raised you. Read the full recipe for Rice and Peas with Oxtail . Rice and peas with oxtail, from Episode 1 Soliat Bada and Michael Famoroti in Episode 1 Episode 2 moves to the Gulf for lamb kabsa, Saudi Arabia’s national dish, fragrant with dried lime and seven spice. Soliat is joined by Bella Adeleke , CEO of Asali Africa and founder of the fashion label Garbe, for a conversation about redefining success. Read the full recipe for Lamb Kabsa . Lamb kabsa, from Episode 2 Still to come are Nigerian fried rice with fried turkey and dodo, cooked with Toyin Jolapamo and Nneoma Mere; jambalaya with Goldie Iyamu and Vanessa Iloenyosi ; and a season finale with Edwin Okolo and Temi Omolehinwa. For more on Asali Africa and the products and ideas it develops, visit asali.africa . Episodes 1 and 2 are out now on YouTube. Watch Episode 1 below. https://www.youtube.com/embed/-6Ux0-vNDnw Sponsored Content The post Asali Africa: Serves Up ‘There’s Rice at Home’ A New Cooking Series Hosted by Chef Soliat Bada appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. item.title: Viral Video: Military uniforms found with bandits not from us – DHQ
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Defence headquarters has denied supplying military camouflage uniforms allegedly found in the possession of suspected bandits in a viral social media video, insisting that the clothing did not originate from the Nigerian military. Read Also: The footage, circulating widely online, showed large quantities of woodland and desert camouflage uniforms spread on the ground, Several others were packed in sacks and allegedly held by suspected bandits. Reacting to the video, the Director of Defence Media Operations, Maj. Gen. Michael Onoja ruled out the possibility that the uniforms were supplied by the military. “That is not possible,” he said, when asked whether the clothing originated from the Nigerian military. Onoja also dismissed suggestions that the uniforms might have been stolen from military supply vehicles attacked by bandits, saying no such incident had been reported. “No such report has been made. It is not from the Nigerian military,” he added. The video reportedly showed two different camouflage patterns, identified as woodland and desert designs, raising renewed concerns over the circulation of military clothing among criminal groups and unauthorised persons. The development comes amid longstanding concerns about criminals, impersonating security personnel to perpetrate attacks, kidnappings and other crimes. In February 2024, the Federal Government reiterated restrictions on the unauthorised use of military camouflage by civilians, warning against the misuse of security uniforms and equipment by criminal elements Minister of State for Defence, Bello Matawalle had stated that the restrictions were necessary to enable security agencies to distinguish legitimate personnel from impostors. He noted that criminals had exploited military and other security agencies’ uniforms to deceive members of the public and facilitate criminal activities. The government’s position was aimed at curbing impersonation, preventing the misuse of military uniforms and strengthening security operations across the country. item.title: Boat capsizes with 300 passengers in Bayelsa
item.description: By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa A tragedy struck the riverine enclave of Southern Ijaw Local Government Area on Friday, as a cargo boat conveying over 300 passengers capsized, leaving many feared dead. The ill-fated vessel was reportedly en route to Ukubie community from Anyama Ijaw, when the incident occurred at 12 noon. According to preliminary reports, the boat, which was heavily overloaded with passengers traveling for a burial ceremony, went down in the waterways between Oweikorogha and Angiama communities. Eyewitness accounts indicate that the tragedy might have been averted. It was learned that some passengers had suggested the boat stop at Oweikorogha to decongest the vessel, but the advice was allegedly ignored. The boat reportedly capsized shortly after departing the community. While the actual casualty figure remains unconfirmed, fears are mounting that the death toll could be substantial given the number of persons on board. Mr. Ipigansi Igoniba, Chairman of the State Maritime Workers Union, confirmed the incident to our correspondent but stated that information regarding the disaster was still hazy. “I cannot give the casualty figure right now. We have sent our members to the scene of the accident and search and rescue efforts for the missing persons are ongoing,” Igoniba said. Rescue operations are currently underway, though independent confirmation of the number of survivors or fatalities is yet to be established. The incident has cast a pall of mourning over the community, highlighting once again the dangers of overcrowding and unsafe travel on the state’s waterways.
