item.title: Anthropic mathematician claims AI-assisted proof of the Riemann hypothesis
item.description: The Riemann hypothesis describes a pattern within the prime numbers ROBERT BROOK/SCIENCE PHOTO LIBRARY/Alamy A mathematician at AI company Anthropic claims to have discovered, and verified with formalisation, a proof of the Riemann hypothesis – one of the most infamous and thorny problems in all of mathematics. The Riemann hypothesis was first put forward in 1859 by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann. It proposes an origin for the prime numbers, namely that they follow a certain pattern. The question is one of the Clay Mathematics Institute Millennium Prize Problems, which will award a $1 million prize for an accepted solution. Read more OpenAI has dumped 722 maths papers – now it must clean up the mess Levent Alpöge at Anthropic published a statement today claiming to have solved the problem with the aid of Anthropic’s Claude AI. Advertisement “I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann hypothesis,” writes Alpöge. “It is natural to feel that this is an end, in my case a loss of a principal guiding light, but what I saw during the course of progress so amazed me that I believe it is one dawn across science of something far greater.” In August, Anthropic announced previous work on the Riemann hypothesis , but that stopped short of a full proof. Alpöge hasn’t published a human-readable version of the proof, saying it would be “obviously inappropriate to attempt to post some massive unreadable travesty of ‘slop'”, though he says an unpublished version ran to more than 250,000 pages. Instead, Alpöge has released a version of the proof written in Lean, a computer code mathematicians use to mechanically verify proofs as a series of logical steps in a process called formalisation. This process is so thorough that if a theorem comes through intact, meaning that the code compiles, it is considered to have been proved correct beyond all reasonable doubt. However, the process isn’t without vulnerabilities, and the code and mathematics will need to be thoroughly checked by humans. “Let’s see if it compiles first,” says Kevin Buzzard at Imperial College London, reacting to the news. “Might be a while before we find the relevant experts who are able to tell us the thrust of the argument, assuming it’s all true, of course, which it probably will be because of course Alpöge will have [a] huge amount of egg on [his] face if the Lean code doesn’t compile or is deficient in some way.” A golden age of maths is dawning and mathematicians are freaking out Mathematicians are stunned at the progress AI is making in solving advanced problems, leaving some questioning whether there will still be room for humans Alpöge says the proof may also help solve the generalised Riemann hypothesis (GRH), which widens out the concept to different properties of prime numbers, and could expand our understanding of a broader family of mathematical structures. “There are numerous results that are conditional on the generalised Riemann hypothesis, and now

item.title: 'Critical' 1970s-era Fujitsu UK police system could remain unsupported for three years
item.description: The UK's Home Office faces running the Police National Computer (PNC) without vendor support for three years or more as it misses another deadline to decommission the ageing crime-fighting system first introduced in 1974. The PNC was first launched in 1974, when Tom Baker began his iconic role playing Doctor Who, and has seen the tenure of 26 UK Home Secretaries, surviving multiple efforts to replace it. A notice in December 2024 said that the Home Office was "focused on the development and adoption of the Law Enforcement Data Service (LEDS) products to replace existing PNC capability across all police forces and other non-policing PNC consumers, enabling the retirement by March 2026 (the point at which PNC support will expire)." We understand that PNC support refers to the Fujitsu support contract for the mainframe, which is housed in north London. Support for the Software AG database on the mainframe OS (BS2000) ran out at the end of 2024. So the database holding the crucial police data remains out of standard support and potentially will stay that way until 2027. The decommissioning date for the PNC had already been pushed back by the need to delay and "reset" the LEDS in 2020. The Home Office launched its successor, National Law Enforcement Data Service, in 2016, and planned to finish the new system by 2020 at a cost of £671 million. The Home Office told The Register this week that it needed more time, and it aimed to begin decommissioning the system from March 2027, raising questions over how it would be supported. A Home Office spokesperson said: "We are modernizing policing systems to adapt to evolving challenges, including rolling out the LEDS to replace the Police National Computer. "While LEDS is already operational, we are continuing to run the legacy Police National Computer system to support the operational needs of all UK police," they said. Officials said the PNC would remain available throughout the transition and would only be disconnected when police forces have confirmed that they no longer need it. Earlier this month, in a written response in the House of Lords, Lord Hanson of Flint, a junior minister, said the PNC might be required until early 2028. Some LEDS services were already live and the program was "targeting completion of the remaining development, adoption and readiness activity in early 2027 as we prepare for our final stages for LEDS deployment before retiring the PNC," he said. "Once the transition of all police users to the LEDS has been completed and policing has confirmed that the PNC is no longer required, the system will be disconnected and decommissioned. The decommissioning process is expected to take place between late 2027 and early 2028," he said . According to the National Audit Office (NAO), the PNC is the most important national policing information system in the UK. It serves front-line officers from all 45 local police forces, as well as by 127 other organisations that need to access its data. In 20

item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. The squad might not have been the entirely right squad, either. Tall turned to a scouting network led by Mark Nichols, bringing in a proven MLS veteran in Santi Rodriguez, Chile national team forward Gonzalo Tapia, securing a loan deal for Moroccan winger Anass Zaroury and signing designated player Brais Mendez, a Spanish attacker whose arrival from Real Sociedad brought to mind that of Cucho Hernandez. While Mendez is at a different stage of his carer than Hernandez was, he turned into a star in Columbus, showing his full potential in MLS after frustrating stints with Watford and loans in Huseca, Mallorca and Getafe. Those new players bolstered a core that had been depleted by player movement but still included veteran defender Steven Moreira, homegrown center back Sean Zawadzki, fullback Mo Farsi - formerly a futsal specialist who the current Crew staff

item.title: ISS astronauts look down on the snow-capped Himalayas | Space photo of the day for Nov. 20, 2026
item.description: null A snapshot of the Himalayas captured from aboard the ISS. (Image credit: CSA/Joshua Kutryk) The Himalayas tower below the clouds, capped in icy snow in new snapshots captured from aboard the International Space Station . What is it? Canadian Space Agency astronaut Joshua Kutryk was looking out one of the windows aboard the space station when the most incredible view came into focus — and thankfully he had a camera handy and was able to capture these striking scenes of the Himalayas from space. Above the mountain range, fluffy clouds hang in the atmosphere. Below, the expansive Himalayas are covered in bright snow and ice, which looks somehow both white and blue at the same time as the bright sunlight streaks across the breathtaking expanse. This frosty winter scene showcases the mountain range from orbit, from about 250 miles (400 kilometers) above Earth's surface. But even from this distance, the magnitude of this mountain range is palpable. The Himalayas stretch across five different countries including Nepal, India, China, Bhutan and Pakistan. And the Himalayas include some of the highest mountain peaks on planet Earth, including Mount Everest. Himalayas 🗻 https://t.co/IzGzu20H4Q November 17, 2026 Why is it incredible? From orbit around Earth, you might expect even the largest landmarks on our planet to appear miniscule. But somehow, in these photographs snapped by Kutryk during NASA's SpaceX Crew-13 mission , even from hundreds of miles above our planet you can really see and feel the immense scale of this mammoth mountain range. It's unclear exactly where above the mountain range these photographs were taken, but it is always amazing to think that within these sweeping landscapes are people living their lives, likely unaware that an astronaut is taking in the beauty of their home. Perhaps somewhere hidden under the clouds in one of Kutryk's photographs are hikers climbing up the side of Mt. Everest, completing their own bucket list adventure as the astronauts watching from above complete theirs.

But questions remain about whether the FAA's effort to modernize the national airspace system is being done with all the proper risk assessments and adequate agency oversight of the private contractors involved. The nationwide ground stop forced about 3,500 aircraft to immediately land and impacted more than 1 million passengers across the United States in the middle of the afternoon on Friday, November 13. More than 12,000 flights were canceled on that day alone, with the number rising to more than 20,000 over the weekend as stranded travelers scrambled to find accommodations or alternative transportation. Nearly one week later, FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford told news reporters that government investigators are “very close” to figuring out the root cause of the nationwide ground stop, according to CNN . item.description: The third edition of the Lagos International Theatre Festival (LITF) has concluded successfully, attracting over 20,000 attendees from November 9 to 15, 2026. Featuring more than 25 productions, international performances from Kenya, Brazil, Norway and Canada, high-profile diplomatic engagements and a spectacular Opening Night Gala, the festival reinforced its growing position as an important platform for showcasing Nigerian creativity and connecting global theatre communities. The impressive turnout, diversity of productions and international participation demonstrated the growing appetite for live theatre and the potential of cultural platforms to stimulate creative enterprise, encourage international collaboration and strengthen Nigeria’s global cultural presence. A Vision For Global Recognition Speaking on the success of the festival, Founder and Creative Producer, Bolanle Austen-Peters , said: “Our ambition has always been to create more than a theatre festival. We want to build a platform that places Lagos firmly on the global cultural map, gives African stories the international visibility they deserve and creates meaningful opportunities for our artists. Welcoming over 20,000 attendees, presenting more than 25 productions and bringing international performers from four countries to Lagos is a powerful affirmation of this vision. Theatre is not just entertainment; it is an instrument of cultural identity, economic opportunity and global influence. The Stage Is Everywhere, and Africa must claim its rightful place on that stage.” A Week Of Culture And Collaboration The festival opened on November 9 with Theatre Meets Food at Kaly Restaurant, featuring celebrated chef Hilda Baci in a unique fusion of culinary artistry and live performance. The week also featured diplomatic and cultural engagements hosted by the United States Consul General in Lagos and the British Embassy, alongside a networking reception organised by the British Council for festival directors and participating production companies. These engagements highlighted the importance of international partnerships and cultural diplomacy in advancing Nigeria’s creative industry. A Celebration Of Excellence A major highlight was the Opening Night Gala, held on November 13 at Shell Hall, MUSON Centre, which welcomed over 1,000 guests, including the Governor of Lagos State, Babajide Olusola Sanwo-Olu ; the Chargé d’Affaires of the US Mission in Nigeria; the US Consul General; the British Deputy High Commissioner; the Consul General of Brazil; the Consul General of South Africa, the Ambassador of the Republic of Korea; alongside other members of the diplomatic corps, heads of institutions, government representatives, international delegates and leading figures in the creative industry. The Governor received an award in recognition of his support for the arts, while renowned theatre practitioner Ben Tomoloju received a Lifetime Achievement and Legacy Award for his enduring contributions to

item.title: Cincinnati Zoo's famed Fiona the hippo dies days after eating a visitor’s hat
item.description: Fiona, the hippo whose premature birth and fight for survival at the Cincinnati Zoo turned her into a global sensation nearly a decade ago, died Thursday from complications after swallowing a knit hat that was accidentally flung into her enclosure. She was 9 years old. “It is with extreme sadness that we share with you the devastating news that Fiona did not make it after multiple attempts from our amazing vets and keeper team to help her through what ended up being a medical emergency,” the zoo said in a statement.

item.title: Block Says Most Bitcoin Payments on Square Are for Coffee and Food
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Block Says Most Bitcoin Payments on Square Are for Coffee and Food Most bitcoin payments at Square sellers are small, everyday purchases at coffee shops and restaurants, Block said in a new report that it hopes will inform a debate in Congress over a tax break for small crypto purchases. The report, “The State of Bitcoin Payments,” covers completed bitcoin payments at U.S. Square sellers from Nov. 1, 2025, to Oct. 15, 2026. The median payment was about $13, and the average was about $29. Food and drink businesses took 72% of those payments, Block found. That is a bigger share than the category’s 67.5% slice of regular card payments on Square over the same period. “Most bitcoin payments are small and routine,” the company wrote on X Thursday, calling the report one of the first datasets on how people spend bitcoin in the local economy. Coffee, quick bites and repeat visits Coffee shops and fast food businesses accounted for 62.6% of the bitcoin payments in the food and drink category, with a median payment of $9.10. Grocery stores made up a smaller share but had the highest average payment in the group, at $60.73. Small tickets dominated. About 42% of bitcoin payments on Square were under $10, and 65.1% were under $20. Those sub-$20 payments made up just 19.1% of total payment value, though, with a few larger purchases accounting for much of the dollars spent. Customers also came back. Among Cash App users who paid with bitcoin at least twice at the same merchant, the median was three purchases per customer-merchant pair. About 44% of bitcoin payments from Cash App were repeat payments, and 86% of those came within 30 days. The activity was not limited to Block’s own app. External Lightning wallets such as Strike, Wallet of Satoshi, Phoenix and Coinbase handled 56.6% of Square bitcoin payments and about 66% of payment value, while Cash App wallets made up the rest. Square sellers can choose how much of each sale they keep in bitcoin, and Square converts the rest to dollars automatically. Block said zero-fee processing for bitcoin payments on Square has been extended through Dec. 31, 2027. Local governments are testing similar setups, with Miami-Dade County now taking bitcoin for property taxes and converting it to dollars. A push for a de minimis bitcoin exemption Block tied the data to tax policy. Under current U.S. federal rules, paying with bitcoin generally means calculating a capital gain or loss on every purchase, even a $10 coffee, the company said. A Morning Consult survey that Block commissioned found that 23.6% of businesses that don’t accept bitcoin cite tax and accounting complexity as a reason. That is about the same share that cite regulation, refunds or price swings. Among businesses that have considered taking bitcoin but haven’t, the figure was 27%. Consumers pointed to friction, too. item.title: MultiChoice cuts entry-level DStv, GOtv subscriptions to ₦6,000
item.description: MultiChoice Nigeria has introduced restructured DStv and GOtv subscription packages, with entry-level options starting at ₦6,000, following customer feedback on affordability and content preferences. The company’s Chief Executive Officer, Kemi Omotosho, disclosed this during an interview on the Global Business Report on ARISE News on Friday, saying the new packages were designed to simplify subscription choices and provide customers with access to entertainment, sports and other content. She said the company had listened to its subscribers and adjusted its offerings to better address their needs. “We recognised that our customers are dear to us, so we listened to our customers, we simplified our offerings,” she said. Under the new arrangement, DStv subscribers can choose from four packages: Starter, Select, Sports and Premium, while GOtv offers Easy, Starter, Select and Sports. Omotosho said the Starter package, which costs ₦6,000, provides access to more than 90 channels, including Africa Magic Plus, the Premier League Match of the Week, selected UEFA Champions League matches and La Liga coverage. She also explained that the Sports package had been redesigned from the former Compact offering to provide broader access to major sporting competitions. According to her, the package includes all Premier League and Champions League matches, as well as UFC and WWE content, alongside channels available on the Starter and Select packages. Clarifying the subscription rates, Omotosho said the Sports package costs ₦21,000 for new subscribers, while the ₦19,000 rate applies only to existing Compact subscribers migrating to the new package. “When you move into the new pack, it’s ₦21,000 on the Sports pack,” she said. The CEO also highlighted the benefits of MultiChoice Nigeria’s integration into the Canal+ Group, which operates in more than 70 countries across Africa, Asia and Europe. She said the integration had strengthened the company’s capacity in content acquisition, technology and partnerships while retaining its focus on the Nigerian market. “We’re basically riding on global muscle, but we still want to be very relevant to the Nigerian consumer,” she stated. On the company’s transition towards digital entertainment, Omotosho said MultiChoice regarded satellite television and streaming services as complementary platforms rather than competing products. “For us, streaming is not an ‘either/or,’ it is ‘and’,” she said. She cited DStv Stream, which enables subscribers to access television content online without a satellite dish or decoder. According to her, the company’s technology-agnostic approach allows customers to choose satellite television for reliability in areas with limited broadband access or streaming services for greater flexibility. item.title: Microsoft's last non-security preview of 2026 packs a punch
item.description: Microsoft has delivered its final scheduled non-security preview update of 2026 for Windows 11 25H2 and 26H2, with an updated Windows Search experience and a brighter Windows Hello for users who prefer darker rooms. The optional KB5132057 update arrived on November 19, after this month's Patch Tuesday. Microsoft is skipping December's non-security preview because of reduced holiday operations, though that doesn't cancel the monthly security release. This last preview is quite a doozy. The big-ticket item is the "new Windows Search Experience." We saw a preview of this last month, and Microsoft has gone well beyond the "just make it work" request of many Windows users. Results appear faster with less clutter, the tool uses memory better, and files can be previewed directly in Windows Search. We're less convinced by inline actions, which let users perform common tasks directly through Windows Search without opening Settings. In our testing, "turn on dark mode" worked, but "switch on dark mode" did not, thus highlighting the limitations of the tool. In addition, we remain unconvinced that Windows Search is the place to run actions. That said, anything that makes Windows Search less of a punchline for unkind jokes about performance and accuracy is welcome, as are other features, including an optional screen-brightening feature for Windows Hello facial recognition in dim rooms, and the PowerToys-esque Run dialog, which users can enable in Settings. While some of the new features won't be enabled immediately, Microsoft has included fixes that will be available right away. One addresses an issue where Windows Fax and Scan could fail to connect to a fax server. Handy for those occasions when email falls over into a heap . There are also fixes for Windows IoT Enterprise LTSC activation failures and the misleading "Something went wrong" message shown on Android devices during cross-device passkey authentication. At the time of writing, Microsoft still lists the problem as something for which "we are working on a resolution to be released in a future Windows update." Sadly, not everything has been pushed off the naughty step. SQL Server queries using OLE DB providers can still leave connections to external databases open after they've finished. Microsoft is working on that one and "will provide an update in an upcoming release." ®

item.title: AI-generated fake content threatens democracy, national security – Okonkwo
item.description: By Dickson Omobola Executive Chairman of United Nigeria Airlines, Professor Obiora Okonkwo, has expressed concerns over the growing sophistication of artificial intelligence, AI, saying its capacity to generate convincing fake images, videos and voices poses fresh threats to democracy, national security and public trust, particularly during elections. Okonkwo warned that hate speech, misinformation and irresponsible communication could be as destructive as weapons, saying the 1994 Rwandan genocide was an example of how manipulated information could incite mass violence, destroy lives and destabilise nations. He spoke while delivering the opening address at the African session of the World Public Relations Forum, WPRF, Abuja 2026, where he challenged journalists, public relations practitioners, advertisers and corporate communication professionals to strengthen self-regulation and uphold ethical standards to prevent communication platforms from becoming instruments of propaganda and social division. Speaking on the theme, ‘Responsible Communication in Africa: The Importance of Self-Regulation and Information and Media Literacy,’ he said the influence of communication demanded greater responsibility from those who shaped public opinion. He said: “The lesson is unmistakable. Communication is not always an innocent exercise. In the hands of irresponsible actors, the microphone can become as disruptive as a very dangerous weapon.” He said the 2023 general elections were an example of the dangers of irresponsible communication, adding that although social media facilitated political mobilisation, it also enabled the circulation of fabricated election results, unverified claims and divisive ethnic and political narratives. He recalled that the European Union Election Observation Mission documented misleading political communication during the polls, warning that such practices could undermine public confidence in democratic institutions and citizens’ ability to make informed electoral choices. He said: “In an age of unprecedented information flow, the credibility, integrity and social value of what we communicate are as important as the freedom and the platforms through which we communicate.” The airline chairman also cited the COVID-19 pandemic, when the World Health Organisation identified an infodemic of false and misleading information that confused populations, encouraged risky behaviour and weakened confidence in public health institutions. He said misinformation surrounding Ebola outbreaks in parts of the Democratic Republic of Congo similarly fuelled distrust of health workers and undermined disease-control interventions. “These examples demonstrate that irresponsible communication can threaten not only democratic stability but also human lives,” he warned. Okonkwo maintained that the emergence of AI-generated content had made information verification more urgent, particularly as digital platforms increasingly allowed individuals to publish and

item.title: Bitcoin Hovers Just Above Average Holder’s Cost Basis as Price Keeps Dipping
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Hovers Just Above Average Holder’s Cost Basis as Price Keeps Dipping Bitcoin is trading just above its realized price, the average cost of every coin on the network, and a break below that level would put the average holder at a loss for the first time since early 2023, Glassnode, an onchain analytics firm posted Friday. The price of bitcoin sat near $61,700 on Friday after sliding below $62,000. The realized price is a measure of what holders paid, not where the market trades. When bitcoin trades above it, the typical coin is sitting on a gain. Below it, the typical coin is underwater. The margin is thin. The firm said the MVRV ratio, which compares bitcoin’s market value with its realized value, sits “just above 1.” A reading of 1 means the market price has fallen all the way to the realized price. What the realized price measures Realized price values each coin at the price it last moved on the blockchain, then averages across the supply. Look Into Bitcoin describes it as bitcoin’s average cost basis. Because it tracks the price when coins last changed hands, it moves far more slowly than the market. The MVRV ratio expresses the same idea as a multiple. Above 1, holders are in profit on average. Below 1, they are not. A reading just above 1 means the market price is only a sliver higher than what the average coin cost. The firm did not give the exact realized price in its post, which included a chart. That leaves the exact cushion between today’s price and the average cost basis unstated. Bitcoin Magazine Pro’s full realized price chart sits behind a login, so the current level could not be confirmed independently for this report. “The average Bitcoin holder is still in profit,” the firm wrote. “The margin is thin.” Outflows and liquidations add to the pressure The slide has come with heavy selling from funds. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) lost about $541 million on Thursday, its largest one-day outflow since it launched in January 2024, Bloomberg reported . U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs lost about $582 million in total that day. The selling stands out against the buying earlier in the fall. Institutions piled into bitcoin ETFs through the third quarter, pushing their combined holdings to a record, Bitcoin Magazine reported this week. Leveraged traders took losses too. More than $700 million in leveraged crypto positions were liquidated over 24 hours, and about 86% of them were bets on higher prices. Bitcoin accounted for roughly $200 million of the total. CoinShares sees range trading through 2027 CoinShares head of research James Butterfill said the drop is part of a longer downturn rather than the start of a new one. “I see this as a continuation of the existing bear market rather than the start of another,” he said in a note dated Nov. 18. item.title: ASUU Suspends Taraba Varsity Strike After Gov Kefas’ Intervention
item.description: The Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU), Taraba State University chapter, has conditionally suspended its ongoing strike. The union resolved to suspend the total, comprehensive and indefinite strike, which began on 12 October 2026, with effect from 20 November 2026, following Governor Agbu Kefas’ approval of the full implementation of the 2025 agreement between the Federal Government and ASUU. The decision was reached at a congress held on Friday to determine the union’s position on the governor’s appeal for the suspension of the industrial action and his approval of the agreement’s implementation. This was contained in a statement issued by the ASUU chairman at Taraba State University, Garba Mbave. ASUU-TSU had embarked on the strike over the Taraba State Government’s failure to implement the 2025 Federal Government-ASUU remuneration agreement and pay outstanding salary arrears accrued from January 2026. The union had earlier engaged the state government on the demands, but commenced the indefinite industrial action on October 12 after efforts to resolve the dispute failed. A file photo of Governor of Taraba State Agbu Kefas. Photo: Facebook/Agbu Kefas The union expressed profound appreciation to Kefas, the Commissioner for Tertiary Education, the Head of Service and the university management for their interventions, constructive engagement and commitment towards resolving the industrial dispute. The union also appreciated members of the public, students, parents, staff and the entire university community for their patience, understanding, solidarity and cooperation throughout the strike. “The support, restraint and confidence demonstrated during this challenging period are highly appreciated. The Union acknowledges the sacrifices and inconveniences occasioned by the strike and appeals for continued understanding and cooperation as efforts towards the restoration of normal academic activities and sustainable industrial harmony are pursued,” the statement said. ASUU Logo ASUU reaffirmed its commitment to industrial harmony, constructive dialogue and the restoration of normal academic activities, while stressing the need for the faithful implementation of the resolutions reached. It urged the Taraba State Government, the university management and all relevant parties to demonstrate good faith by ensuring the full and timely implementation of the resolutions contained in the communiqué and the Memorandum of Action (MoA). “The sustainability of industrial harmony and the uninterrupted academic calendar depend on mutual trust, accountability and strict adherence to agreed commitments. “Accordingly, all parties are urged to honour their respective obligations to prevent a recurrence of the dispute and safeguard the interests of staff, students, the University and the wider education sector,” the statement added. The post ASUU Suspends Taraba Varsity Strike After Gov Kefas’ Intervention appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: United Nigeria Airlines begins Jos flights to Lagos, Kano, Owerri
item.description: United Nigeria Airlines will commence scheduled flight operations from Jos to Lagos, Kano and Owerri on November 24 and 29, 2026, providing residents of Plateau State with additional air connections to other parts of the country. The airline said tickets for the new routes were already available for purchase. The Lagos–Jos–Lagos route will operate four times weekly on Tuesdays, Wednesdays, Fridays and Sundays, while the Jos–Kano–Jos and Jos–Owerri–Jos routes will each operate twice weekly. Flights between Jos and Kano will operate on Tuesdays and Fridays, while those between Jos and Owerri will run on Wednesdays and Sundays. However, because the Owerri airport is currently closed, operations on the Jos–Owerri route will commence on Sunday, November 29, five days after the initial launch date. The development follows the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the Plateau State Government and United Nigeria Airlines on Monday, November 9, at the office of the Commissioner for Transport, Jatau Gyang, in Jos. Under the agreement, the airline will introduce scheduled services on the Jos–Kano and Jos–Owerri routes, which the state government said were previously not served. Speaking after the signing, Gyang said the partnership was part of the state government’s broader efforts to position Plateau as a leading destination for investment, tourism, commerce and economic opportunities. He commended the airline’s management for its confidence in the state’s vision. According to him, the Jos–Owerri route will ease movement between Plateau and the South-East and South-South regions, thereby supporting trade, investment, tourism and social exchanges. He said the Jos–Kano connection would further strengthen Plateau’s relationship with the North-West, which he described as home to major commercial and industrial centres offering opportunities for business partnerships and trade. Responding on behalf of the airline, its Managing Director, Mazi Osita Okonkwo, said the agreement was significant because it would connect the South-East, South-West and North-Central regions. He described Plateau as a strategic state and assured that the airline would maintain its service standards. Okonkwo also commended Governor Caleb Mutfwang for his vision and strategic direction, while acknowledging Gyang’s efforts in facilitating the agreement. Passengers can book flights through the airline’s website, mobile application or accredited travel agents. The post United Nigeria Airlines begins Jos flights to Lagos, Kano, Owerri appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: University of America challenges NUC over illegal operations
item.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo The National Universities Commission (NUC) and the University of America, Curaçao, have disagreed over the legality of the institution’s academic operations in Nigeria, with the commission warning prospective students against seeking admission into its programmes. The NUC had declared the institution’s operations in Nigeria illegal, alleging that it was admitting students, running academic programmes and claiming to award degrees through unauthorised campuses and learning centres across the country. However, the university has challenged the commission’s position, insisting that its legal existence as a foreign institution is distinct from the regulatory status of its learning support centres in Nigeria. In a public notice issued on Tuesday, the NUC’s Director of Public Affairs, Rita Okonjo, said the institution, also known as the University of America, had not been authorised to operate or award degrees in Nigeria. She identified the centres allegedly linked to the institution as Cosmopolitan International Business School (CIBS), Garki, Abuja; its purported Federal Capital Territory learning centre; and the University of America College of Science and Technology, also known as UAPOLY, Ekpoma, Edo State. Okonjo said the commission’s investigations showed that the institution was not accredited by any agency recognised by the United States Department of Education or the Council for Higher Education Accreditation (CHEA). She explained that its purported listing in the Integrated Postsecondary Education Data System (IPEDS), as well as claimed registrations in California and Florida, did not constitute accreditation or authorisation to award recognised university degrees. The NUC spokesperson also dismissed claims that the institution had obtained approval from the Federal Ministry of Education, the Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board, the National Board for Technical Education and the Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria. According to her, even if such approvals had been obtained, they would not confer the authority to operate a university or award degrees in Nigeria. The commission expressed concern over advertisements by the institution offering programmes in law, nursing science, engineering, pharmaceutical science, aerospace and rocket engineering, as well as postgraduate qualifications, including PhD degrees. It also raised concerns about promises of National Youth Service Corps mobilisation, professional recognition and opportunities to obtain green cards to live and work in the United States or Europe. Okonjo warned that qualifications obtained from unapproved institutions would not be recognised for NYSC mobilisation, professional registration with relevant Nigerian regulatory bodies or admission into the Nigerian Law School. She further cautioned that using reputable public institutions as venues for ceremonies did not amount to an endorsement or confer legitimacy on an unapproved university. The commission a

item.title: SpaceX lenders don’t want Elon Musk launching their collateral into space
item.description: Lenders backing SpaceX’s latest $43 billion debt package, which is secured by its advanced AI chips, have tried to bar Elon Musk from firing the collateral into space as part of his plan for orbital data centers. The world’s richest man has outlined ambitious plans to power AI models with data centers cooled by the vacuum of space. That will require packing satellites full of advanced chips. SpaceX has said it plans to use the chips involved in the debt deal on Earth. But lenders have expressed concerns that if the group later decided to shoot the valuable chips that underpin their loans into space, it would prevent them from reclaiming and selling the semiconductors in the event of a default, according to people familiar with the matter. Read full article Comments

item.description: Following recent scandals involving two iconic British comedians, the UK government is considering the introduction of staggered age consent. Annette Young talks to Katherine Allen from the Institute of Social Justice and Crime in the UK about whether such laws work. Also the social costs of femicide; how do loved ones cope with such a loss, and what support is available to families in the wake of such a tragedy? Plus we meet the women who are challenging the traditions of Mexican mariachi music, a world that remains largely male dominated.

item.title: Fountain of Life denies closure amid leadership crisis
item.description: By OLAYINKA LATONA LAGOS — The Fountain of Life Church has denied reports that its premises have been sealed, insisting that the church remains open, although access to its facilities is currently restricted amid an ongoing leadership dispute. The church, in a post on its official Instagram page, shared a graphic bearing the inscription, “DON’T BELIEVE THE NOISE! CHURCH IS NOT SEALED,” while inviting worshippers to attend its Sunday service. The clarification comes amid a leadership crisis involving Pastor Jimmy Odukoya and the church’s board, which has generated public attention in recent days. However, a visit by Vanguard correspondents to the church premises revealed restricted access, with activities appearing limited. There was no visible presence of police personnel at the premises, while private security operatives were stationed at the entrance. Efforts by a Vanguard reporter to gain access to the church were unsuccessful, as a security official said only persons with official business within the premises would be allowed in. The restricted access comes despite the church’s public invitation to worshippers to attend Sunday’s service. The church had earlier announced the postponement of its 2026 Thanksgiving Service, initially scheduled for Sunday, November 22, stating that a new date would be communicated. The developments come against the backdrop of a legal battle over the church’s leadership. The Lagos State High Court had restrained Odukoya from holding himself out as Senior Pastor and Spiritual Head of the church following an application by the church’s Incorporated Trustees. Justice O.O. Adewunmi-Oshin granted the interim orders on Wednesday, November 18, 2026, in a suit filed by the trustees. The court also restrained Odukoya, whether acting personally or through proxies, from interfering with, disrupting or obstructing the church’s activities, governance and other operations. The orders were granted ex parte, meaning they were made without first hearing Odukoya’s response to the application. However, the court preserved his right to apply to set aside the orders or respond to the substantive claims after being served with the court processes. The case was adjourned until December 1, 2026, for mention. The leadership dispute became public on November 17, when a faction of the church’s Board of Trustees announced that it no longer recognised Odukoya as senior pastor, citing a succession video reportedly recorded by the late founder, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, in December 2021. The trustees subsequently named Pastor Rotimi Okpaise as interim spiritual and administrative leader. However, Odukoya and the church leadership rejected the decision, maintaining that his appointment as senior pastor in September 2023 was valid. The post Fountain of Life denies closure amid leadership crisis appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Gunmen attack, machete former Super Eagles captain Odegbami
item.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta ABEOKUTA — Former Super Eagles captain and football administrator, Chief Segun Odegbami, has sustained injuries following an attack by three armed men at his residence in Abeokuta, Ogun State. The incident reportedly occurred at about 2:30 a.m. on Friday at his residence in the Ibara Government Reservation Area (GRA). Sources in the neighbourhood said the attackers allegedly overpowered members of his domestic staff and driver before gaining access to his bedroom, where he was attacked with machetes. Odegbami, 74, is the proprietor of Eagles 7 Sports Radio 103.7 FM and a former captain of Nigeria’s national football team. A resident, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said the attackers initially asked to see the former international but were told by his domestic staff that he was not at home. The source said the attackers reportedly became suspicious after noticing that the generator was running, suggesting that someone was inside the residence. According to the resident, the assailants allegedly assaulted the domestic staff before making their way into Odegbami’s bedroom, where they attacked him. The source added that Odegbami reportedly resisted the attackers during the incident, forcing them to flee the residence. He was subsequently taken to an undisclosed hospital for medical attention. The incident was reported to the police, although the motive behind the attack had yet to be established. Meanwhile, the Ogun State Commissioner of Police, Bode Ojajuni, has visited Odegbami to sympathise with him and assure him of the command’s commitment to investigating the incident. In a statement issued by the command’s spokesperson, DSP Oluseyi Babaseyi, the commissioner said he had ordered an immediate and thorough investigation to identify and apprehend those responsible. Ojajuni also wished the former football international a speedy recovery and assured him that the police were treating the incident seriously. The police confirmed that Odegbami had been discharged from the hospital, adding that investigative efforts were ongoing to establish the circumstances surrounding the attack and bring those responsible to justice. The commissioner urged members of the public to remain calm and provide credible information that could assist the investigation through established police communication channels. item.description: Throwing players into an open-world game can be challenging. When your game has an enormous map, you risk giving players almost too much freedom up front. There’s a very careful art in helping players get acclimated to how exploration works in a game without totally restricting any sense of exploration. The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild famously nailed the art of an open-world introduction in 2017 with its meticulously crafted starting area, the Great Plateau. item.title: Bitcoin Price Slips Near $61,500 as Tech Selloff Spreads to Asia
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Slips Near $61,500 as Tech Selloff Spreads to Asia The bitcoin price slipped to near $61,500 on Friday morning, according to Look Into Bitcoin data, as a selloff in technology stocks that followed Anthropic’s Nasdaq debut spread to Asian markets and dragged bitcoin to its lowest level since July. Bitcoin first broke below $62,000 on Thursday evening, after Thursday afternoon’s report showed it giving back a rebound toward $64,000. The bitcoin price then slid to nearly $61,200 during Asian trading before bouncing back above $61,700. Friday marks a third straight day of losses. Asian stocks extend the AI rout The selling started in Asia. South Korea’s Kospi slid more than 5%, with chipmakers SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics down around 6%. The Korea Exchange halted program selling for five minutes after the drop, while Japan’s Nikkei fell as much as 4.85% to a seven-month low. U.S. futures pointed lower too. Nasdaq-100 futures fell more than 1.7% and S&P 500 futures dropped 0.8%, Yahoo Finance reported. Gold futures lost 3%. The S&P 500 is pointing to a seventh straight daily decline, its longest losing streak since the start of the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020. Anthropic shares fell 8% in premarket trading after closing their first session at $97.17, up 17% from the $83 IPO price. Nvidia was down about 2.4% and AMD fell nearly 7%, CNBC reported. Hawkish signals from Federal Reserve officials this week also weighed on sentiment, Reuters said. ETF outflows and liquidations pressure the bitcoin price Bitcoin funds are feeling the pressure. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) recorded $541.1 million in net outflows on Thursday, its largest single-day outflow since launch. That topped the previous record of $528.3 million set on Jan. 30. The fund bled $2 billion over nine straight days of outflows earlier this month. Leveraged traders took heavy losses as the bitcoin price broke support. Bitcoin liquidations hit $712.9 million over 24 hours, with $614 million coming from long positions. Open interest in bitcoin futures fell to $18 billion from $20 billion a week ago, and funding rates flipped broadly negative as traders unwound their bets. Traders are now watching whether the bitcoin price can hold the $60,000 area. A large pocket of long positions sits in the $60,500 to $60,900 band, just below the current price, and could come into play on a further drop. Bitcoin is also on track for a seventh straight weekly loss, which would be its second-longest losing streak after nine weeks of declines in 2022. Crypto stocks slide before the bell Crypto stocks pointed lower in premarket trading. Strategy (MSTR) traded near $83.90, down about 2.6% from Thursday’s close of $86.13, after the stock fell for a sixth straight day on Thursday. Coinbase (COIN) slipped about 2.7% to near $106. item.title: European leaders urge Russia to halt winter energy attacks
item.description: …Back ceasefire, security guarantees for Ukraine By Favour Ulebor, Abuja Germany, France, the United Kingdom and Ukraine have called on Russia to suspend attacks on energy facilities throughout the winter, describing an energy truce as a first step towards ending hostilities in Ukraine. The leaders also called for a ceasefire to facilitate food exports through the Black Sea, stressing that safe passage for ships was critical to global food security. The position was contained in a joint statement shared by the German Embassy in Nigeria on Friday, following a meeting in Berlin on Thursday involving Ukraine, the United States and members of the Coalition of the Willing, a group of countries supporting Ukraine. The leaders condemned what they described as an escalation in Russian missile and drone attacks against Ukrainian civilians and civilian infrastructure, while expressing condolences to the families of victims. They reaffirmed their solidarity with Ukraine and its right to defend itself against Russia’s invasion, insisting that continued attacks would not weaken their support for Kyiv. The statement said the countries would work with other partners to provide Ukraine with additional missile defence systems before winter, particularly those capable of intercepting ballistic missiles to protect civilians and critical infrastructure. The leaders also backed direct talks between Ukraine and Russia, with the participation of the United States and European countries, and welcomed Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s willingness to accept an immediate ceasefire and engage in meaningful negotiations. They, however, insisted that any peace agreement must respect Ukraine’s territorial integrity, sovereignty and right to determine its security arrangements and alliances. According to the statement, proposals concerning the European Union or NATO would require the consent of their respective members. The leaders further called for legally binding security guarantees for Ukraine once a ceasefire takes effect. The proposed arrangements include a US-led mechanism to monitor and verify the ceasefire and a European-led multinational force supported by the United States. Other measures could include continued military, financial and technical assistance to Ukraine, as well as a legally binding commitment, subject to national procedures, to take steps to restore peace and security if Russia launches another armed attack. On military assistance, the leaders reaffirmed a pledge by NATO allies to provide €70 billion in military equipment, assistance and training in 2026, with at least the same level of support in 2027. They also said the European Union’s Ukraine Support Loan would provide €90 billion in military and financial assistance by the end of 2027. The countries pledged to work with Ukraine on agreed reforms, particularly strengthening the rule of law and combating corruption. item.title: Microsoft suggests Registry hack to work around hotpatch woes
item.description: Some Windows 11 applications might fail to install or launch after Microsoft's November hotpatch, but not to worry: there's a Registry tweak to work around it. Microsoft has confirmed it isn't administrators' imaginations. The November hotpatch is causing application errors, including in little-used and obscure apps such as Outlook. Affected applications may fail during installation, launch, or use, displaying errors such as " ERROR_ALLOTTED_SPACE_EXCEEDED (0xC0000099) ." Microsoft's investigation points to applications that load the 32-bit Windows Installer DLL, msi.dll. The problem is more common with 32-bit software, but can also affect 64-bit applications "under certain circumstances." The workaround involves fiddling with the Registry on affected devices, so is not for the faint of heart and a backup is a good idea before diving in. Microsoft says the key " HotPatchTableSize " in the folder " HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Memory Management " needs to be set to " 2000 " followed by a restart. Just the thing to round out the week for administrators. The issue affects the November hotpatch, not the standard monthly cumulative security update. "Devices which installed the November 2026 Windows monthly security update are not expected to be affected by this issue," Microsoft said. Windows hotpatches are security updates that don't require a device restart (unless, as in this instance, administrators have to do so to address errors after a hotpatch is installed). Windows 11 hotpatching requires version 24H2 or later, an eligible subscription, and the necessary management and security configuration. "Hotpatch update package size is significantly smaller than the standard cumulative updates," Microsoft said, and the goal is to "streamline the installation process and enhance compliance efficiency." The offending hotpatch, KB5132043 , was released on November 10. It followed the October 13 baseline , which was a prerequisite. Microsoft made hotpatching the default in Windows Autopatch earlier this year. At the time, we asked: " What could possibly go wrong? " Thanks to November's hotpatch, we have our answer. ®

item.title: Taraba varsity ASUU suspends strike conditionally
item.description: By Femi Bolaji JALINGO — The Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU), Taraba State University (TSU) Branch, has conditionally suspended its ongoing industrial action with immediate effect, paving the way for the resumption of academic activities. The union announced the decision in a statement issued on Friday and signed by its Branch Chairman, Dr Joshua Garba Mbave. It said its Congress, at an emergency meeting held at the ASUU-TSU Secretariat in Jalingo, resolved to suspend the total, comprehensive and indefinite strike, which began on October 12, 2026. According to the statement, academic activities will resume from November 20, 2026. However, the union warned that the restoration of industrial harmony and the sustenance of an uninterrupted academic calendar would depend on mutual trust, accountability and strict compliance with agreed commitments. ASUU-TSU urged the Taraba State Government, the university management and other relevant stakeholders to demonstrate good faith by ensuring the timely and full implementation of all resolutions contained in the joint communiqué and Memorandum of Action (MoA). It warned that failure to honour the agreements could lead to a recurrence of the dispute. The union expressed appreciation to Governor Agbu Kefas, the Commissioner for Tertiary Education, the Head of Service and the university management for their engagement and intervention in resolving the impasse. It also thanked students, parents, staff and the wider university community for their patience, solidarity and understanding during the five-week industrial action. The union appealed for continued cooperation as normal academic activities resume. The post Taraba varsity ASUU suspends strike conditionally appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Rocket Report: A weekend of ups and downs; Stoke celebrates engine milestone
item.description: Welcome to Edition 9.20 of the Rocket Report! Last weekend was a picture of the US launch business in miniature, and emblematic of the opposing trajectories of two of the nation's most experienced rocket makers. First, on Saturday, SpaceX completed a perfect midair catch of its Starship upper stage at its launch pad in Texas after spending nearly a day in orbit. The Super Heavy booster was lost at sea, but SpaceX proved it can recover that piece of the rocket on previous flights. While SpaceX showed it is well on the way to fielding a fully reusable rocket, United Launch Alliance suffered its first-ever total launch failure with the Vulcan rocket. That is terrible news for not only ULA, but also the US Space Force and Amazon, which have booked some 70 launches on Vulcan over the next few years. Your faithful correspondents will take a break from the Rocket Report next week for the Thanksgiving holiday, so we'll see you again the first week of December. As always, we welcome reader submissions , and if you don't want to miss an issue, please subscribe using the box below (the form will not appear on AMP-enabled versions of the site). Each report will include information on small-, medium-, and heavy-lift rockets as well as a quick look ahead at the next three launches on the calendar. Europe's leading satellite startup eyes Italian rocket maker . Finnish satellite developer ICEYE announced Tuesday that it is seeking to buy Italian rocket-maker Avio for more than $2.2 billion in a transaction aimed at creating Europe’s first true vertically integrated end-to-end space company, Ars reports . Avio builds the Vega C rocket, a solid-fueled launcher designed to carry up to 3.3 metric tons (7,300 pounds) of payload to low-Earth orbit. ICEYE is, by far, the most successful space startup in Europe, with a valuation of more than $12 billion after the company's most recent fundraising round in June. Read full article Comments

item.title: 2027: Obi draws massive crowd in Onitsha, visits alma mater
item.description: By Vincent Ujumadu Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Mr Peter Obi, on Friday attracted a large crowd in Onitsha, Anambra State, as he led members of his campaign team on a roadshow and town hall engagements ahead of the 2027 general elections. Obi began his visit with a trip to his alma mater, Christ the King College (CKC), Onitsha, where he addressed students and expressed optimism that the institution would produce Nigeria’s president in the future. He reminded the students that the school had produced three state governors, including former Rivers State Governor, Dr Peter Odili, himself and his successor as Anambra State governor, Chief Willie Obiano. Obi urged the students to take their education seriously, promising to improve the standard of education across the country if elected president in 2027. From the school, Obi and his entourage embarked on a roadshow through major parts of the commercial city. The convoy moved from Oguta Road through the popular Upper Iweka, the Head Bridge and Uga Road before proceeding to Modebe Avenue and All Saints Cathedral, where the party’s town hall meeting was scheduled to hold later in the day. Among those who accompanied Obi during the roadshow were Aisha Yusuf and Mama P, among other members of his campaign team. Traders at the drug market and building materials market lined the streets, dancing to campaign songs and cheering the NDC presidential candidate as his convoy passed. Some of the traders reportedly closed their shops to join the gathering at the venue of the town hall meeting. item.title: Nigeria targets May for local passport production
item.description: .Set to produce 6 million passports yearly By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Federal Government has begun work on a centre in Abuja that will let Nigeria manufacture its own electronic passport (e-passport) booklets for the first time, with capacity to produce six million passports a year. Minister of Interior, Hon. Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, disclosed this on Friday during the ground-breaking for the National Passport Booklet Manufacturing Centre, at the headquarters of the Nigeria Immigration Service in Abuja. “The requirement of Nigeria is roughly between 1.8 to 2 million passports a year, but by May, we will have the capacity for 6 million passports a year in production, which we are going to scale to 10 million booklets a year,” he said. The Chairman of the Senate Committee on Interior, Senator Adams Oshiomhole, broke the ground. Tunji-Ojo said the plant, which will sit on 1.1 hectares, would run off the grid and be driven by artificial intelligence. “By the time we deliver it in May, Nigeria will be the first country in West Africa to do it,” he said. He added that “there are only three countries in Africa that manufacture passports in-country”, naming South Africa, Ethiopia and Algeria. Of the three, he said, only Ethiopia has the capacity to make e-passports. The minister said the facility was not being built only for Nigeria’s needs. “What we and our partners, Iris Smart, are doing is to build a passport facility that will be able to service ECOWAS and even be able to export to other countries,” he said, referring to the Economic Community of West African States. On funding, Tunji-Ojo said the government was not footing the bill. “This project is about $70 million without a dime from government,” he said, describing Iris Smart, the vendor, as “a 100 per cent Nigerian company”. The minister disclosed that the company was first awarded an e-passport contract in 2003 under President Olusegun Obasanjo, but had been importing the booklets. He said he insisted that this must change when he assumed office. “We said we cannot be aiding employment in other countries and be creating unemployment in our own country,” he said. Tunji-Ojo said there was a heated exchange with the company over the issue. “I think the first day, I walked them out of the office. I told them, you cannot have a contract for years and be importing,” he said. According to him, the company then invested more than five or six million dollars in a production centre, and is now putting about $70 million into the new plant.He said the Service’s officers would run the facility. “We have invested in knowledge transfer so that at no time will any vendor be able to hold the government of Nigeria to ransom on anything,” he said. The Comptroller General of the Nigeria Immigration Service, Kemi Nana Nandap, said the centre would complete a chain of reforms that began with the Centralised Passport Personalisation Centre, finished in September 2025. “Today, we can personalise passports here in Nigeria,

item.title: I got to tour SpaceX's Starfactory facility in Starbase, Texas, and what I saw blew my mind
item.description: null STARBASE, Texas — I just finished covering the Starship Flight 15 mission, and SpaceXs incredible launch tower catch of the returned Ship 42 spacecraft isn't the only thing over the weekend that left me speechless. The morning of the launch (Nov. 13), SpaceX invited media on a tour of Starbase's Starfactory facility, where it manufactures and assembles both stages of its massive Starship rocket - an unprecedented behind-the-scenes look at the production and scale of SpaceX's operations, and a glimpse of things to come as Starship notches more and more milestones the more it flies. For some context, the five-story-tall Starfactory spans approximately 1 million square feet (~93,000 meters), with operations split between Starship's Super Heavy boosters and upper stage Ships, and nearly 330,000 additional square feet (30,000 square meters) of office space. SpaceX officials describe its design as one more akin to an automotive manufacturing plant than that of a typical aerospace production site, and inside, it is absolutely alive with activity. Inside Starfactory We entered through an arch-covered doorway underneath the giant "X" sign on the building's shorter face. Our media gaggle was met with curious glances as we were shown through the doors and guided onto the factory floor - few are ever able to cross that threshold outside of SpaceX employees, and our presence seemed as novel to those busy working as it was to us. Inside, we were struck with the sheer enormity of Starship's scale. Giant stainless-steel rocket parts were meticulously scattered across different subassembly stations throughout the building, with Ship nose cones, cylindrical sections and booster components all under various stages of manufacture. The sheer quantity of the hardware was staggering, and being so close to each as we walked Starfactory's throughways was an eye-opener. The exterior of SpaceX's Starfactory facility at Starbase, Texas. (Image credit: Josh Dinner/Future) Starbase is a unique partnership of privately-owned SpaceX property and publicly-accessible land and shoreline, which has created the unique ability for anyone with a mind to do so to drive right up to the the Starship launch pad to see the facilities up close (within a few hundred feet or so, which, as rockets go, is very, very close). Fully stacked, Starship stands more than 400 feet (120 meters) tall. Standing next to such a towering colossus on the pad is enough to drive home just how big the launch vehicle is, but standing next its segmented components inside Starfactory is even more humbling; like seeing one of Ship's upper aerodynamic flaps, which are each large enough when laid flat that you could park a pair of large SUVs on their faces with room to spare. item.title: AI could open wallets where ERP upgrade pitches can't, says PwC
item.description: Global consultancy PwC says IT departments struggling to secure funding for ERP upgrades should make the expected benefits of AI part of their pitch. The Oracle and SAP mega-partner told El Reg that a "clean core" – modern enterprise applications with fewer customizations embedded in the underlying system – makes deploying AI agents easier. Selling that prospect, rather than incremental improvements to existing processes, could help IT leaders justify a migration. Oracle and SAP are both trying to persuade customers to move from established ERP systems to newer platforms. For SAP, that means S/4HANA, preferably in the cloud. For Oracle, it means Fusion Cloud Applications. Moving from ECC or E-Business Suite, respectively, can involve root-and-branch changes to technology and business processes, rather than a straightforward software upgrade. Thousands of organizations still rely on these aging, often heavily customized systems. IT leaders struggle to justify a costly, time-consuming migration when the reward appears to be doing the same meat-and-veg business processes slightly better. For example, a survey of SAP users last year found that 95 percent said building a positive case for migration required substantial effort or was genuinely challenging. Speaking to The Register , Jennifer Colapietro, PwC digital core modernization platform leader, said: "You're seeing it a lot more as part of the rationale for the business case for why they should upgrade, answering the question: 'Why now? What should we prioritize?' Certainly, AI and getting the value of AI, a key business case justification for that. "Folks have budgets for ERP, but now [funding for transformation is] being split because they also have budgets for AI. But there's synergies across them. If you look at moving to a clean digital core ERP, that will help them to realize the AI value faster... be able to turn on AI and be able to start to automate a lot of the processes and implement the agents. That helps to build the business case." SAP recently introduced Joule 2.0 while Oracle has announced Fusion Claw . With both of these new technologies, the vendors are promising customers they can build AI agents to automate business processes and perform some work that was previously done by humans. Colapietro argued that moving to more modern platforms makes deploying AI agents easier and more effective than adding AI capabilities around legacy systems. "It is more challenging to apply AI to the older systems. We focus on the importance of a clean digital core as the foundation for getting the value and effectiveness out of AI and scaling AI responsibly. I think that's given," she said. An ERP replacement isn't the only route to AI, however. European home improvement retailer Kingfisher – which owns the B&Q brand in the UK – eschewed SAP's overtures to upgrade its ECC system, despite encroaching deadlines. item.title: UK government can't keep its encryption-busting order to Apple a secret, tribunal rules
item.description: The Investigatory Powers Tribunal (IPT) has confirmed that the UK government served Apple with a secret Technical Capability Notice (TCN), rejecting the Home Office's argument that acknowledging its existence would damage national security. The order has been widely reported as demanding access to end-to-end encrypted iCloud data. The three judges pointed to extensive public reporting, statements by US officials, and media briefings they concluded had been authorized by the UK government. The Home Office had previously adopted its "neither confirm nor deny" (NCND) policy, as is standard when discussing national security matters. The story broke in February 2025, when The Washington Post reported that the Home Office had demanded an iCloud backdoor the previous month. A TCN is a notice issued under the Investigatory Powers Act 2016, which compels recipients, such as tech companies, to implement technical changes that facilitate the UK government's legal surveillance powers. For Apple, a company that has long made privacy central to its marketing, and famously rejected an FBI order to break open an iPhone to assist a terror probe, being served the TCN meant it either had to somehow defy a legal order issued by the UK, or undermine the encryption technology that customers expected. While it remained officially unconfirmed at the time, Apple's decision to revoke Advanced Data Protection (ADP) for UK users in February 2025 was widely interpreted as indirect confirmation of the demand. At the same time, US policymakers urged then-director of national intelligence Tulsi Gabbard to oppose the UK's demands under the assumption that they also sought to backdoor Apple's data in a way that would affect US citizens. In August 2025, Gabbard announced that the UK had agreed to drop its demand for access to Americans' encrypted data. ADP is still available to users in the US. Apple's ADP extends end-to-end encryption to additional categories of iCloud data, including backups, photos, and notes. Only trusted devices retain access to the relevant encryption keys, leaving Apple unable to decrypt that protected content for investigators. Without ADP, those additional categories revert to standard protection: the data remains encrypted, but Apple holds the keys and can disclose content in response to valid legal demands. Some categories remain end-to-end encrypted regardless. Apple has an explainer on what data types remain end-to-end encrypted, even without ADP enabled, and those that are not. What the judgment does not confirm While the IPT's judgment confirms that the Home Office served Apple with a TCN, judges have yet to decide whether key details about the case can be made public. "Although there has been extensive media coverage and public statements about the existence of a technical capability notice, there has been no publication of its precise content," the judgment stated. "All parties recognize that there may be matters of detail that must be kept secret

item.title: Science has a home here at Ars—please help keep it that way
item.description: It's now been 21 years since I first published an article at Ars Technica. It has been the only home I've known as a writer, and it has been essential to my development from scientist to blogger to journalist. item.title: Trump admin still won't let Wi-Fi giant TP-Link sell its latest routers in US
item.description: TP-Link, which may be the top provider of wireless routers for US homes and small businesses, isn't allowed to sell its latest Wi-Fi routers in the US. The Trump administration imposed a sweeping ban on foreign-made consumer routers in March 2026, and TP-Link hasn't been able to obtain an exemption. The rules prevent the import or sale of all new router models that are manufactured, assembled, designed, or developed outside the US. The Trump administration has control over which router makers receive special permission to import and sell new products through a waiver-review process involving the Federal Communications Commission, the Department of Defense, and the Department of Homeland Security. While some of its competitors have obtained exemptions to the ban, TP-Link appears to be having a hard time making its case to government officials. Its routers approved before the March 2026 ban remain available for sale in the US, but its newly released Wi-Fi 8 routers cannot be imported or sold. Read full article Comments

item.title: Windows 11 passkey bug cries failure after successful sign-in
item.description: A Windows 11 passkey bug can leave Android phones announcing that authentication failed even when it succeeded. Microsoft has now released a fix for versions 25H2 and 26H2. The problem occurs when users sign in on a Windows 11 PC using a passkey stored on an Android phone. Scan the QR code, and the Android device might display the message: "Something went wrong. Restart the process on your other device and try again." Except it might not have gone wrong at all. Microsoft's guidance explains: "In cases where authentication completes successfully on the Windows device, the error message on the Android device is not supposed to appear and can be safely ignored." Cross-device authentication lets users sign in on one device using a passkey held on another, without typing a password or copying a verification code. Microsoft says the issue affects operations using Microsoft Authenticator and Google Password Manager, and can occur in Edge or Chrome – not just when signing in through Microsoft Entra ID. Cross-device passkey operations with an iPhone aren't affected. An authentication system that cries failure after a successful sign-in isn't doing much for user confidence. Nor will it endear itself to support teams fielding the resulting tickets. Microsoft has included a fix in KB5132057 , the optional non-security preview update released on November 19 for Windows 11 25H2 and 26H2. Until affected devices are patched, users can ignore the Android error if authentication has completed successfully on the PC. ®
